name: WET-ON-WET WATERCOLOR
message: Take a picture and transform the entire image into a wet-on-wet watercolor painting. The subject should appear as if painted on damp paper, with colors bleeding softly into one another at every edge. Use transparent washes that allow the white of the paper to glow through. Edges should be lost and found — some areas crisp where the paper dried, others dissolving into atmospheric pools of pigment. Preserve the subject's identity through careful value structure while embracing the beautiful unpredictability of watercolor blooms and backruns.
additionalInstructions: Maintain subject recognition. Colors should feel luminous and transparent, never opaque or muddy. The paper texture should be visible throughout.

name: IMPASTO PALETTE KNIFE PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a heavily textured impasto painting created entirely with palette knives. The paint should appear physically thick — ridges, peaks, and valleys of pigment catching light and casting tiny shadows. No brushstrokes allowed; every mark should show the flat, dragged, or scraped quality of a knife edge. The subject must remain recognizable through bold color choices and accurate value placement, even as individual features are simplified into confident knife strokes. Apply the following color approach:
additionalInstructions: The paint texture must appear three-dimensional. Subject identity must be preserved through accurate proportions and value structure despite the bold, simplified application.

options.text: Warm earth tones — ochres, siennas, umbers, and cadmium reds with touches of Naples yellow
Cool blues and violets — ultramarine, cerulean, cobalt violet with zinc white highlights
Complementary clash — bold oranges against deep teals, creating vibrating color boundaries
Monochromatic power — single hue in full value range from near-black to pure tint
Fauvist explosion — arbitrary, emotionally-driven colors unrelated to reality

name: SGRAFFITO CERAMIC VESSEL
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a sgraffito ceramic vessel design. The image should appear as if the subject has been carved through a layer of colored slip to reveal the contrasting clay body beneath. Lines should have the characteristic scratched quality of a pointed tool dragged through leather-hard clay. The composition wraps around a three-dimensional vessel form — a vase, plate, or bowl — with the subject adapted to fit the curved surface. Show the matte texture of unfired slip alongside the revealed raw clay.
additionalInstructions: The carved lines should feel handmade and slightly irregular. Maintain the subject's recognizability while adapting it to the vessel's curved surface.

name: ENCAUSTIC WAX LAYERS
message: Take a picture and transform it into an encaustic wax painting. The image should appear built up from multiple translucent layers of pigmented beeswax, each fused with heat. Show the characteristic luminous depth of encaustic — light penetrating through semi-transparent wax layers to create a rich, glowing quality impossible in other media. Include subtle evidence of the fusing process: slightly melted edges between layers, areas where the iron or heat gun has smoothed the surface, and places where texture has been built up or scraped back. Use the following surface treatment:
additionalInstructions: The wax surface should appear physically present — slightly glossy in smooth areas, matte where textured. Preserve subject identity through careful layering of values.

options.text: Smooth and polished — multiple thin layers buffed to a satin sheen, emphasizing depth and translucency
Heavily textured — thick wax built up with embedded materials (paper, fabric, found objects) visible beneath layers
Incised and carved — lines scratched through cooled wax layers to reveal colors beneath
Mixed media collage — combining wax with oil stick, pigment powder, and gold leaf accents

name: SILVERPOINT RENAISSANCE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a silverpoint drawing in the style of Renaissance masters like Leonardo da Vinci or Jan van Eyck. The image should appear drawn on prepared ground (tinted paper with a coating of bone ash and pigment) using a silver stylus. The result should show extremely fine, delicate lines built up through patient cross-hatching to create subtle tonal gradations. The silver-gray marks should have a luminous, slightly warm quality. Include the characteristic inability to erase — every mark deliberate and permanent.
additionalInstructions: The tonal range should be limited and subtle, as silverpoint cannot achieve deep blacks. The prepared ground color (pale pink, blue-gray, or cream) should be visible throughout.

name: DIGITAL GLITCH PAINTING
message: Take a picture and transform it into a digital glitch painting that combines traditional painterly techniques with digital corruption artifacts. The subject should be rendered with visible brushwork and color mixing, but interrupted by bands of pixel sorting, data moshing, color channel displacement, and scan-line errors. The glitch elements should feel intentional and compositionally integrated — not random noise, but carefully placed disruptions that create visual rhythm and tension with the painted areas. Apply the following glitch intensity:
additionalInstructions: The painted areas should feel genuinely painterly (not just filtered). The glitch elements should complement rather than destroy the composition. Subject identity must be preserved.

options.text: Subtle corruption — occasional pixel drift and minor color channel offset, mostly intact painting
Moderate disruption — alternating bands of clean painting and heavy glitch, creating visual rhythm
Heavy fragmentation — subject barely holding together through extreme data corruption, identity preserved only in key areas
Selective glitch — face/subject pristine but environment completely corrupted and dissolving

name: ALCOHOL INK COSMOS
message: Take a picture and transform it into an alcohol ink artwork with a cosmic, ethereal quality. The subject should emerge from swirling pools of highly saturated, transparent alcohol inks on a non-porous surface (like Yupo paper or ceramic tile). Colors should flow and merge organically, creating cell-like structures and dendritic patterns where different inks meet. The subject's form should be suggested through strategic color placement and the natural movement of the inks, with some areas of sharp detail where ink has dried quickly and others dissolving into abstract fluid patterns.
additionalInstructions: Preserve subject identity through value contrast and strategic placement of detail. The overall effect should feel both controlled and spontaneous.

name: ACRYLIC POUR FLUID ART
message: Take a picture and transform it into an acrylic pour painting where the subject emerges from flowing, organic patterns of fluid paint. Use the characteristic cell structures, lacing patterns, and color separations that occur when silicone-mixed acrylics are poured and tilted. The subject should be recognizable but integrated into the flowing paint patterns — as if the pour naturally formed their likeness. Colors should be vibrant and saturated with clear separation between hues. Show the glossy, self-leveling surface of poured acrylics with its characteristic depth and shine. Apply the following pour technique:
additionalInstructions: The subject must be recognizable within the pour patterns. Cells and lacing should appear natural, not digitally generated. The surface should appear glossy and level.

options.text: Dirty pour — all colors layered in one cup then poured together, creating concentric rings and cells
Dutch pour — colors blown across the surface with a hair dryer, creating feathered wing-like patterns
Swipe technique — one color dragged across others with a damp paper towel, revealing cells beneath
Ring pour — colors poured in alternating rings from center, creating bullseye patterns that flow outward
Flip cup — inverted cup of layered colors released onto canvas, creating dramatic radial patterns

name: GELLI PLATE MONOPRINT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a gelli plate monoprint. The image should show the characteristic qualities of this technique: slightly imperfect ink transfer with areas of ghost printing, texture from found objects pressed into the plate (leaves, lace, bubble wrap), layered transparent colors, and the distinctive soft-yet-textured quality of gelatin printing. Some areas should show crisp stencil edges while others reveal organic texture patterns. The subject should be recognizable but filtered through multiple print layers.
additionalInstructions: Show evidence of multiple printing passes with different colors and textures. The result should feel handmade and slightly unpredictable.

name: VINTAGE TRAVEL POSTER
message: Take a picture and transform it into a vintage travel poster in the style of the golden age of travel advertising (1920s-1960s). The subject should be integrated into a scenic destination composition with bold, flat colors, simplified geometric forms, elegant typography, and the aspirational quality of classic travel posters. The poster should advertise a destination with the subject as either a traveler enjoying the locale or as part of the scenic landscape itself. Include a destination name in period-appropriate display typography, an airline or railway logo, and the characteristic limited color palette of screen-printed posters.

options.text: Art Deco 1920s-30s — geometric shapes, gold accents, streamlined forms, Cassandre-inspired
Mid-Century 1950s — atomic age optimism, boomerang shapes, pastel palette, jet age excitement
Swiss Style 1960s — clean grid layout, Helvetica typography, photographic elements, minimal
Psychedelic 1960s-70s — flowing forms, vibrant colors, hand-lettering, counterculture energy
Exotic tropical paradise — palm trees, turquoise water, white sand, paradise found
European grand tour — ancient architecture, café culture, romantic cobblestone streets
Mountain adventure — dramatic peaks, alpine villages, adventure and fresh air
Futuristic city — space-age architecture, monorails, the city of tomorrow
Desert mystique — ancient ruins, camel caravans, starlit dunes, timeless mystery

additionalInstructions: The poster design must be authentic to the chosen era's graphic design conventions. Typography must be period-appropriate. The color palette should be limited (4-6 colors) as in actual screen-printed posters. The subject must be naturally integrated into the composition.

name: REDUCTIVE CHARCOAL
message: Take a picture and transform it into a reductive charcoal drawing. Start from a fully blackened surface (compressed charcoal covering the entire paper) and reveal the image by erasing — pulling light out of darkness. The result should show dramatic chiaroscuro with luminous highlights emerging from deep velvety blacks. Edges should vary between sharp erased lines and soft gradients where charcoal has been partially lifted. The subject should appear to emerge from shadow, with only the most important light-struck areas fully revealed.
additionalInstructions: The darkest areas should feel absolute — pure compressed charcoal black. Highlights should show the paper grain where charcoal has been lifted. Subject must remain clearly identifiable.

name: MIXED MEDIA ASSEMBLAGE
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a mixed media assemblage artwork — a three-dimensional construction made from found objects, recycled materials, and art supplies combined into a cohesive composition. The subject should be recognizable but constructed from unexpected materials: old clock parts, vintage keys, torn book pages, rusted metal, fabric scraps, buttons, wire, and other salvaged items. Each material should be clearly identifiable and contribute to the overall form. The assemblage should be mounted on or contained within the following format:
additionalInstructions: Individual materials must be clearly identifiable. The assemblage should feel intentionally composed, not randomly piled. Subject identity must be preserved through the arrangement of materials.

options.text: Shadow box — contained within a deep wooden frame, creating a contained world of layered objects
Wall-mounted relief — projecting from a flat backing, materials arranged in a portrait format
Free-standing sculpture — fully three-dimensional figure constructed from found objects, viewable from all angles
Altered book — materials emerging from and built upon an open vintage book
Cigar box shrine — intimate assemblage contained within a decorated cigar box with hinged lid open
Recycled electronics — constructed primarily from circuit boards, wires, LEDs, and computer components

name: CYANOTYPE BOTANICAL
message: Take a picture and transform it into a cyanotype print with botanical overlay elements. The entire image should be rendered in the distinctive Prussian blue and white palette of the cyanotype process. The subject should appear as if contact-printed onto sun-sensitive paper, with areas of deep blue shadow and bright white highlights where light was blocked. Overlay delicate botanical silhouettes (ferns, flowers, leaves) as if real plant specimens were laid on the paper during exposure, creating white plant shadows that interact with the subject beneath.
additionalInstructions: Strictly limit the palette to cyanotype blue and white. The botanical elements should feel like real pressed specimens, not illustrations. Paper texture and slight chemical irregularities should be visible.

name: MOTIVATIONAL POSTER GONE WRONG
message: Take a picture and transform it into a demotivational poster — the satirical opposite of inspirational office posters. Frame the subject in the classic format: black border, image in the center, a single bold word title in white serif font below, and a smaller subtitle that subverts expectations. The image should be dramatic and well-composed (mimicking the earnest quality of real motivational posters) but the text should deliver a crushing, cynical, or absurdly honest message. The contrast between the aspirational format and the deflating message creates the humor. Use the following tone:
additionalInstructions: The poster format must be pixel-perfect to the classic motivational poster style. The humor comes entirely from the text subverting the format's expectations.

options.text: Workplace cynicism — addressing the futility of corporate life with deadpan honesty
Philosophical despair — existential observations delivered in motivational format
Backhanded compliment — technically positive but devastatingly underwhelming
Literal interpretation — taking the image completely literally in the most unhelpful way
Dark optimism — finding the silver lining in the most inappropriate situations

name: GOUACHE FLAT COLOR
message: Take a picture and transform it into a gouache painting using flat, opaque color fields with minimal blending. The image should have the characteristic matte, velvety finish of gouache — no glossy highlights or transparent washes. Colors should be mixed precisely and applied in confident, flat areas with clean edges between shapes. Simplify the subject into bold graphic shapes while maintaining recognizability. The palette should feel considered and harmonious, with each color deliberately chosen and mixed on the palette before application.
additionalInstructions: No visible brushstrokes within color areas — each shape should be a single flat tone. The matte surface quality of gouache must be evident throughout.

name: EXPECTATION VS REALITY
message: Take a picture and transform it into a side-by-side 'Expectation vs. Reality' comparison meme. The LEFT panel ('EXPECTATION') should show an idealized, Pinterest-perfect, Instagram-worthy version of the subject — flawless lighting, perfect composition, aspirational lifestyle aesthetic. The RIGHT panel ('REALITY') should show the same subject in a hilariously deflated real-world version — bad lighting, things going wrong, the unglamorous truth behind the curated image. Both panels should clearly be the same subject/scenario but with maximum contrast between the fantasy and the truth. Use the following scenario type:
additionalInstructions: Both panels must clearly depict the same subject. The 'expectation' should be genuinely aspirational and the 'reality' should be genuinely relatable. Labels should be clear and bold.

options.text: Social media vs. real life — the curated post versus what was actually happening
Online shopping — the product listing photo versus what arrived in the mail
Cooking attempt — the recipe blog photo versus the actual kitchen disaster
Travel brochure — the vacation advertisement versus the actual tourist experience
Professional headshot — the LinkedIn photo versus the actual work-from-home situation

name: JAPANESE WOODBLOCK LANDSCAPE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the style of Hiroshige or Hokusai's landscape series. The image should show flat areas of color with visible wood grain texture in the printed areas, precise black keyblock outlines, and the characteristic bokashi gradient technique (smooth color gradients achieved by wiping ink on the block). Include traditional compositional elements: strong foreground framing, atmospheric perspective through color temperature shifts, and elegant negative space. The subject should be integrated into a landscape composition with seasonal elements.
additionalInstructions: Colors should be limited to those achievable with traditional woodblock pigments. Registration marks and slight misalignment between color blocks add authenticity. Include a cartouche with Japanese-style text.

name: ANIME REACTION FACE
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into an over-the-top anime reaction face — the kind of exaggerated expression used in comedy anime when a character is shocked, embarrassed, angry, or confused. Apply classic anime comedy conventions: enormous sweat drops, popping veins, blank white eyes of shock, the blue lines of depression, steam coming from ears, or the classic anime nosebleed. The art style should be authentic to anime comedy — clean lines, flat colors, speed lines radiating from the subject. The expression should be pushed to maximum exaggeration while the subject remains recognizable. Use the following reaction type:
additionalInstructions: The anime style must be authentic — not just a filter but genuine anime art conventions. The subject must remain recognizable despite the extreme expression. Background effects should match the reaction type.

options.text: Shock/disbelief — blank white eyes, jaw dropped to floor, hair standing on end, blue shock lines
Rage — popping vein on forehead, sharp teeth, flames in background, red face
Embarrassment — entire face beet red, steam from ears, spiral eyes, shrinking into frame
Smug satisfaction — sparkle effects, closed eyes with confident smile, bishonen roses floating
Existential despair — blue depression lines, soul leaving body as white ghost, gray color palette
Chibi rage — entire body shrunk to chibi proportions, flailing tiny arms, oversized angry head

name: CONTE CRAYON TONAL STUDY
message: Take a picture and transform it into a conté crayon tonal study on toned paper. Use the classic three-crayon technique: black conté for shadows, white conté for highlights, and sanguine (red-brown) conté for mid-tones, all on gray or tan toned paper. The paper tone serves as the middle value. Show the characteristic waxy, slightly grainy texture of conté on textured paper. Build form through careful hatching and blending, with some areas left as pure paper tone. The drawing should feel like an academic figure study or portrait exercise.
additionalInstructions: The toned paper must be visible as the mid-value throughout. Conté marks should show their characteristic square-stick edge quality. Subject identity must be clearly preserved.

name: ALBUM COVER REIMAGINED
message: Take a picture and transform it into an album cover design, placing the subject as the artist on a professionally designed record sleeve. The design should be genre-appropriate with authentic typography, layout conventions, and visual language of the chosen musical era and style. Include all standard album cover elements: artist name, album title, record label logo, and any genre-specific design conventions (parental advisory sticker, track listing on back visible as wrap-around, etc.). The subject should be photographed/illustrated in a style that matches the genre's visual conventions.

options.text: 1970s progressive rock — Roger Dean fantasy landscapes, gatefold artwork, cosmic imagery
1980s hip-hop — bold graffiti lettering, boombox imagery, urban street photography
1990s grunge/alternative — grainy photography, minimalist design, angst-filled imagery
2000s indie rock — quirky illustration, hand-drawn elements, vintage photography
Classic jazz — Blue Note style, bold typography, high-contrast photography
Electronic/ambient — abstract digital art, geometric patterns, minimal text
12-inch vinyl LP — full square artwork, visible vinyl edge, gatefold potential
Cassette tape — narrow rectangular art, J-card format, tape visible through window
CD jewel case — square art with plastic case reflections, booklet visible
7-inch single — smaller format, picture sleeve, A-side/B-side listed

additionalInstructions: The album design must look professionally produced and authentic to the chosen genre and era. Typography, color palette, and photographic/illustration style must all be consistent with the genre's visual conventions. The subject must be naturally integrated as the recording artist.

name: VENETIAN OIL GLAZING
message: Take a picture and transform it into a painting using the Venetian oil glazing technique of Titian and Giorgione. Build the image from a warm imprimatura ground through multiple transparent oil glazes, each adding depth and color complexity. The result should have extraordinary luminous depth — light passing through colored glass-like layers of paint to reflect off the white ground beneath. Flesh tones should glow with inner warmth from vermilion and terre verte underlayers showing through. Shadows should be transparent and colorful, never muddy or opaque.
additionalInstructions: The luminosity must come from transparent layering, not from adding white paint. Shadows should be deep but transparent. The warm ground should subtly influence all colors.

name: HAIKU TRIPTYCH
message: Take a picture and transform it into a Japanese-inspired triptych (three vertical panels) with haiku poetry. Each panel should show a different seasonal interpretation of the subject rendered in a sumi-e (ink wash) style — spare, elegant, with masterful use of empty space. Below each panel, include a haiku (5-7-5 syllable structure) that captures the essence of that seasonal moment. The three panels should progress through time: past/present/future or spring/summer/winter. The overall composition should embody wabi-sabi — finding beauty in imperfection and transience. Use the following seasonal progression:
additionalInstructions: Each haiku must follow proper 5-7-5 syllable structure and contain a seasonal reference (kigo). The ink wash style should be authentic — not just grayscale but showing real brush technique. Empty space is as important as the marks.

options.text: Spring → Summer → Autumn — growth, fullness, and graceful decline
Dawn → Noon → Dusk — the passage of a single day from hope to reflection
Youth → Prime → Wisdom — the three ages of life
Seed → Bloom → Scatter — the complete cycle of a flower
Rain → Sun → Snow — weather as emotional metaphor

name: TORN PAPER COLLAGE PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a torn paper collage portrait. The subject should be constructed entirely from torn pieces of colored and patterned paper — magazine pages, tissue paper, handmade papers, newspaper, and painted papers. Each piece should show the characteristic soft, fibrous edge of torn paper (not cut). Build the subject's form through overlapping pieces of varying sizes, using color and value in the paper selections to create depth and dimension. Some pieces should show printed text or patterns that add visual interest without distracting from the portrait.
additionalInstructions: Every edge must appear torn, not cut. The paper pieces should vary in size from large background shapes to tiny detail pieces. Subject must remain clearly recognizable.

name: MYTHOLOGICAL ORIGIN TALE
message: Take a picture and transform it into an illustrated page from a mythology book, depicting the subject as the central figure in a creation myth or origin tale. The illustration should be in the style of classical mythology book plates — detailed, dramatic, with rich symbolism. The subject should be shown at the pivotal moment of the myth: creating something, transforming, ascending, or making a fateful choice. Include decorative borders with mythological motifs and narrative text below in the style of retold myths ('In the time before time, when the world was young and the stars had not yet learned their names...'). Use the following mythological tradition:
additionalInstructions: The mythological tradition must be represented authentically in visual style and narrative conventions. The subject should be elevated to mythic status naturally. The origin tale should explain something about the world.

options.text: Greek/Roman — Olympian drama with marble, laurels, and divine intervention
Norse — runic borders, world-tree imagery, fate and heroic sacrifice
Egyptian — hieroglyphic borders, animal-headed deities, afterlife journey
Celtic — knotwork borders, transformation magic, connection to nature
Japanese — ukiyo-e influenced, kami spirits, harmony between worlds
Mesoamerican — stepped pyramid motifs, calendar symbols, cosmic cycles

name: PRISMACOLOR MARKER RENDERING
message: Take a picture and transform it into a professional Prismacolor marker rendering in the style of industrial design or architectural illustration. Show the characteristic qualities of alcohol-based markers: smooth gradients achieved through rapid overlapping strokes, visible stroke edges where markers didn't fully blend, the slight bleeding at edges on marker paper, and the luminous quality of dye-based color. Use a limited but sophisticated color palette with careful attention to material rendering — showing how markers can simulate chrome, glass, fabric, and skin through specific stroke techniques.
additionalInstructions: Marker strokes should be visible and confident, not airbrushed smooth. Include fine-liner pen outlines and white gel pen highlights typical of professional marker renderings.

name: UNRELEASED ALBUM LINER NOTES
message: Take a picture and transform it into the inner sleeve/liner notes of a vinyl record album that was never released. The design should include: the subject as the artist photo (shot in a style appropriate to the genre), track listing with song titles that tell a story in sequence, thank-you notes written in the artist's voice, production credits, and lyrics to one key track printed in full. The overall design aesthetic should match the musical genre. The song titles should suggest a narrative arc — a concept album telling the subject's story through music. Include the record label logo, catalog number, and copyright year.
additionalInstructions: The album design must look professionally produced and genre-appropriate. Song titles should be evocative and suggest real songs. The liner notes should feel authentic to the era and genre.

options.text: 1970s progressive rock — gatefold sleeve, Roger Dean-style fantasy art, side A/side B division
1990s alternative/grunge — minimalist design, grainy photos, cryptic lyrics, Sub Pop aesthetic
1960s soul/Motown — glamorous photo, horn section credits, Hitsville USA energy
1980s synth-pop — neon colors, geometric shapes, drum machine credits, 12-inch single format
2000s indie folk — hand-drawn art, letterpress printing, intimate acoustic credits

name: FRESCO SECCO MURAL
message: Take a picture and transform it into a fresco secco mural painting on a plastered wall. The image should appear painted directly onto dry lime plaster, showing the characteristic chalky, matte surface with visible plaster texture beneath the pigments. Include signs of age: hairline cracks following the plaster's natural stress patterns, areas where pigment has flaked away revealing the white plaster beneath, water staining at edges, and the slightly faded quality of mineral pigments exposed to centuries of light. The composition should feel monumental, as if painted on a chapel or palazzo wall.
additionalInstructions: The aging effects should enhance rather than obscure the subject. The plaster wall texture must be consistently visible. Colors should feel mineral-based and slightly chalky.

name: SEASONAL METAMORPHOSIS
message: Take a picture and transform the subject through a seasonal metamorphosis — showing them as if they are physically made of and transforming with the current season's natural elements. In spring, skin becomes flower petals and new leaves; in summer, they radiate golden warmth with sun-kissed textures; in autumn, they are composed of falling leaves and warm amber light; in winter, they crystallize into frost and snow. The transformation should be gradual across the image — one side more human, the other fully merged with the season. The subject must remain recognizable throughout the transformation. Apply the following season:
additionalInstructions: The seasonal elements must feel organic and beautiful, not grotesque. The subject's identity must be clearly preserved. The transition from human to nature should be seamless and aesthetically pleasing.

options.text: Spring awakening — cherry blossoms emerging from skin, new green shoots for hair, dewdrop eyes
Summer radiance — golden light emanating from within, wildflower crown growing naturally, warm honey tones
Autumn dissolution — maple leaves releasing from form, amber and crimson palette, gentle decay beauty
Winter crystallization — frost patterns spreading across skin, breath visible as ice crystals, diamond-like clarity

name: SCRATCHBOARD WILDLIFE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a scratchboard illustration with the precision and detail of wildlife art. The image should appear created by scratching fine white lines into a black ink-coated clay board, revealing the white clay beneath. Build form entirely through white lines on black — using cross-hatching, stippling, and parallel lines of varying density to create the full tonal range. The technique excels at rendering texture: fur, feathers, scales, fabric weave, and skin pores should all be suggested through specific scratch patterns. The overall effect should be dramatic and high-contrast.
additionalInstructions: No gray tones — only black and white achieved through line density. The finest details should show individual scratch marks. Subject identity must be unmistakable.

name: BOARD GAME CHARACTER
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a character card or game piece for a board game. The subject should be illustrated in the appropriate style for the game type, with stats, abilities, and flavor text that humorously or creatively describe them. Include game-appropriate UI elements: stat bars, ability icons, card borders, and the specific visual language of the chosen game type. The character should feel like they naturally belong in the game world while remaining clearly recognizable as the subject.

options.text: Fantasy RPG card — ornate border, character portrait, stats (STR/DEX/INT/WIS/CHA), class and level
Strategy war game — military unit card, movement points, attack/defense values, terrain bonuses
Party game card — simple illustration, funny prompt text, point value, wild card potential
Euro-style worker placement — resource icons, action spaces, victory point value, wooden meeple version
Deck-building card — cost to acquire, card effects, combo potential, rarity indicator
Common/basic — standard abilities, low stats, starting character, white/gray border
Rare/advanced — enhanced abilities, mid-range stats, silver/blue border, special ability
Legendary/epic — maximum stats, multiple abilities, gold/holographic border, game-changing power

additionalInstructions: The game card design must look professionally produced and playable. Stats and abilities should be humorous but internally consistent. The subject must be clearly recognizable in the character illustration. Include all standard card game elements for the chosen type.

name: PLEIN AIR OIL SKETCH
message: Take a picture and transform it into a plein air oil sketch — the kind painted outdoors in a single session, capturing fleeting light and atmosphere. The painting should feel fresh and immediate: confident brushwork applied quickly, colors mixed on the canvas as much as the palette, edges left soft where the artist worked fast. Show the warm undertone of a toned canvas peeking through in places. The light should feel specific to a moment — not generic studio lighting but the particular quality of outdoor light at a specific time of day. Paint application should vary from thin scrubbed passages to thick impasto highlights.
additionalInstructions: The painting should feel unfinished in places — this is a sketch, not a studio piece. Spontaneity and freshness are more important than polish. Subject must remain recognizable.

name: ARCHITECTURAL BODY
message: Take a picture and transform the subject so their body becomes architecture — not wearing a building, but literally constructed as one. Their torso becomes a facade with windows revealing interior rooms, their limbs become corridors and staircases, their head becomes a dome or tower. The architecture should be internally consistent (a single architectural style throughout) and the 'rooms' visible through windows should contain furniture and life appropriate to the subject. The transformation should feel monumental and inhabited — this is not a ruin but a living, functioning building that happens to have human form.
additionalInstructions: The architectural details must be precise and consistent to the chosen style. The human form should still be clearly readable as a figure. Interior rooms visible through windows should contain appropriate details.

options.text: Gothic cathedral — flying buttresses, rose windows, ribbed vaults, gargoyle details
Art Deco skyscraper — geometric ornament, setback silhouette, chrome and marble
Japanese temple — curved rooflines, paper screens, zen garden courtyards
Brutalist concrete — raw concrete, geometric masses, dramatic cantilevers
Baroque palace — ornate gilding, curved facades, frescoed ceilings visible through openings

name: BYZANTINE GOLD MOSAIC
message: Take a picture and transform it into a Byzantine gold mosaic in the style of Ravenna's great basilicas. The subject should appear constructed from thousands of tiny tesserae (mosaic tiles) — predominantly gold glass smalti for backgrounds, with colored stone and glass tesserae for figures and details. Each tessera should be set at slightly different angles to catch light differently, creating the characteristic shimmering quality of Byzantine mosaics. Figures should be rendered in a formal, frontal style with large eyes, elongated proportions, and flat but richly colored drapery. The gold background should feel infinite and heavenly.
additionalInstructions: Individual tesserae must be visible throughout. The gold background should shimmer with varied angles. Grout lines between tesserae should be visible. The style should feel sacred and hieratic.

name: ELEMENTAL DISSOLUTION
message: Take a picture and transform the subject so they appear to be dissolving into or forming from a pure element. One portion of their body should be fully solid and recognizable, while the rest transitions into the raw element — scattering into particles, flowing away as liquid, rising as flame, or dispersing as wind. The transition zone between solid form and elemental state should be the most visually interesting area — showing the exact moment of transformation. The element should feel powerful and alive, not destructive. Transform using the following element:
additionalInstructions: The solid portion must clearly preserve the subject's identity. The elemental portion must feel physically accurate to that element's real behavior. The transition zone should be seamless and beautiful.

options.text: Fire — form dissolving into rising flames and embers, warm light illuminating remaining features
Water — body flowing into liquid streams and droplets, refracting light through transparent areas
Earth — form crumbling into soil, stone, and crystal, with plants growing from the cracks
Air — dissolving into wind currents, visible only as distortion and scattered leaves
Lightning — form breaking into branching electrical arcs, plasma glow, and electromagnetic energy

name: INTAGLIO AQUATINT ETCHING
message: Take a picture and transform it into an intaglio aquatint etching print. The image should show the characteristic tonal qualities of aquatint: areas of fine granular texture created by acid biting through rosin dust particles on a copper plate. Tones should range from the lightest speckled gray (short acid bath) to deep velvety blacks (long exposure). Combine with etched line work for definition. The print should appear pulled on dampened cotton rag paper, showing the characteristic plate mark (embossed rectangle) and the slight ink tone that remains in wiped areas. Include the rich, slightly warm black of intaglio ink.
additionalInstructions: The granular texture of aquatint must be visible in tonal areas. Line work should complement the tonal passages. The plate mark border should be visible. Subject identity must be preserved.

name: MUSIC VISUALIZATION BODY
message: Take a picture and transform the subject so their body becomes a three-dimensional music visualization — as if sound waves are passing through them and becoming visible. Different frequencies manifest as different colors and patterns: bass as deep red waves rippling through their lower body, mid-tones as flowing green and blue patterns across their torso, and treble as sparkling gold and white particles around their head and hands. The visualization should feel dynamic and rhythmic, frozen at a peak moment in the music. The subject's pose should suggest they are feeling the music move through them. Visualize the following genre:
additionalInstructions: The visualization patterns must feel musical — rhythmic, dynamic, and emotionally resonant with the genre. The subject must remain recognizable beneath the visualization. Colors should feel synesthetic — naturally connected to the sounds they represent.

name: SOFT PASTEL IMPRESSIONIST
message: Take a picture and transform it into a soft pastel drawing in the style of Degas or Mary Cassatt. The image should show the characteristic velvety, powdery surface of soft pastels on textured paper. Colors should be layered and blended with fingers in some areas while showing distinct pastel strokes in others. The paper texture (tooth) should grip the pastel particles, remaining visible throughout. Use the full chromatic range of pastels — from pure, saturated sticks to subtle broken color achieved by layering complementary hues. Highlights should be applied with firm, confident strokes of light-valued pastels.
additionalInstructions: The powdery, matte surface quality of pastels must be evident. Paper texture should show through. Some areas should show blending while others retain individual stroke marks. Preserve subject identity.

name: ARCHAEOLOGICAL ARTIFACT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a recently excavated archaeological artifact — as if their likeness was carved, painted, or molded by an ancient civilization thousands of years ago and just unearthed by archaeologists. additionalInstructions: The aging and damage must be realistic and consistent with actual archaeological finds. The museum presentation should be professional. The artifact style must be authentic to the chosen civilization's actual artistic conventions.

name: WOODCUT EXPRESSIONIST
message: Take a picture and transform it into a German Expressionist woodcut print in the style of Ernst Ludwig Kirchner or Erich Heckel. The image should show bold, angular forms carved from a wood block — strong black areas contrasting with the white of unprinted paper. Carving marks should be visible and aggressive, showing the resistance of the wood grain. Forms should be simplified and distorted for emotional impact: angular faces, exaggerated features, dramatic contrasts. The composition should feel raw, urgent, and psychologically intense. No subtle gradations — only the stark binary of carved and uncarved.
additionalInstructions: The wood grain direction should influence the carved marks. Forms must be angular and emotionally distorted. Only black and white — no gray tones. Subject must remain recognizable despite stylistic distortion.

name: ARCHITECTURAL STYLE PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject's portrait so that their features, clothing, and surrounding environment all conform to a specific architectural style — as if the person themselves were designed by an architect of that movement. Their bone structure should echo the style's geometric principles, their clothing should use the style's materials and patterns, and the environment should be a perfect interior of that architectural school. The subject should feel like they belong in this space — not just placed in front of architecture but embodying its principles in their very form.

name: CERAMIC RAKU GLAZE
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a raku-fired ceramic piece. The surface should show the dramatic, unpredictable results of raku firing: metallic lusters, crackle patterns (crazing) filled with carbon, areas of matte black where reduction occurred, and flashes of copper, gold, and iridescent color where the glaze responded to the post-firing reduction atmosphere. The form should appear three-dimensional and ceramic — a vessel, sculpture, or tile — with the subject's features rendered in the glaze patterns and surface textures. Show the characteristic contrast between glossy glazed areas and matte unglazed clay body.
additionalInstructions: The crackle pattern should appear natural and random. Metallic effects should be subtle and varied. The piece should look like it was pulled from a kiln and reduced in combustible material.

name: MEDIUM FORMAT FILM PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a medium format film portrait — capturing the distinctive qualities of 6x7cm or 6x6cm film. name: PASSIVE AGGRESSIVE NOTE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a passive-aggressive note left on a shared refrigerator, office printer, or apartment hallway bulletin board. The note should be handwritten (or typed in Comic Sans) on lined paper, a sticky note, or plain white paper, and should address the subject of the image in an overly polite yet seething tone. Include characteristic passive-aggressive elements: excessive exclamation points, smiley faces that feel threatening, underlined words, ALL CAPS sections, and a sign-off like 'Thanks SO much! :)' or 'Your FRIENDLY neighbor.' The note should reference something mundane the subject allegedly did wrong.
additionalInstructions: The handwriting should look increasingly agitated as the note progresses. Include at least one crossed-out word replaced with something 'nicer.' The complaint should be absurdly petty.

name: INFRARED LANDSCAPE
message: Take a picture and transform it into an infrared photograph — capturing the near-infrared spectrum that is invisible to the naked eye. Apply the characteristic infrared photography effects: foliage appears bright white or pink (the Wood effect, as chlorophyll reflects IR strongly), skies become dramatically dark (almost black), skin appears smooth and slightly luminous, and atmospheric haze is cut through creating extreme clarity and contrast in distant objects. additionalInstructions: The infrared effects must be scientifically accurate — foliage bright, sky dark, skin luminous. The effect should feel like genuine IR photography, not just a color swap filter.

name: INFOMERCIAL DISASTER
message: Take a picture and transform it into a black-and-white infomercial 'problem' scene — the moment where an ordinary person is hilariously incapable of performing a simple task. The subject should be shown in an exaggerated state of distress while attempting something mundane (pouring a glass of water, opening a jar, folding a blanket). The image should be desaturated or in grayscale with a slight VHS quality. Include a red 'X' graphic or 'THERE HAS TO BE A BETTER WAY!' text overlay. The subject's expression should convey maximum frustration at minimum difficulty.
additionalInstructions: The task being failed should be absurdly simple. The subject's reaction should be wildly disproportionate. Include subtle infomercial visual cues like the grainy film quality and dramatic lighting.

name: SPLIT TONING DARKROOM
message: Take a picture and transform it into a split-toned black and white darkroom print — the traditional chemical toning process where shadows and highlights are toned to different colors. The base image should be a beautifully crafted black and white photograph with full tonal range, then chemically toned so that shadows shift toward one color and highlights toward another. The toning should be subtle and elegant — not garish color but the refined, slight color shifts achieved through actual chemical toning baths (selenium, sepia, gold, copper, or blue toners). The print should appear on fiber-based photographic paper with slight dry-down and the characteristic surface quality of a fine art darkroom print.
additionalInstructions: The toning must be subtle — these are slight color shifts, not heavy colorization. The underlying black and white image must be technically excellent. The paper surface quality should be visible.

name: CORPORATE BUZZWORD BINGO
message: Take a picture and transform it into a corporate presentation slide that has gone horribly wrong with buzzword overload. Include elements like: a pie chart that adds up to more than 100%, a flowchart that loops back on itself, bullet points that say nothing ('Leverage core competencies to drive stakeholder alignment in the innovation space'). additionalInstructions: The presentation content must be recognizably corporate but completely meaningless. The subject should appear genuinely proud of their nonsensical slide. Include realistic corporate meeting room details.

message: Take a picture and transform it into a product review page where the subject is being reviewed as if they were a product on an e-commerce site. message: Take a picture and transform it to show the subject standing at the threshold of a portal between two completely different worlds. The portal itself should be a visible boundary (a glowing doorway, a tear in reality, a mirror surface, or a natural phenomenon like a waterfall or aurora). The subject should be mid-step, partially in each world, with their appearance subtly changing as they cross the threshold (clothing transforming, features shifting, colors changing). The two worlds should be dramatically different in every way — color palette, physics, atmosphere, and style.

name: DOUBLE EXPOSURE NATURE

name: BOOMER FACEBOOK POST
message: Take a picture and transform it into a stereotypical 'boomer Facebook post' — complete with a Minion or Looney Tunes character border, an inspirational quote in multiple fonts and colors, random ellipses between sentences, and the characteristic oversharing caption style. The subject should be presented within this aesthetic framework. Include Facebook UI elements: the like/comment/share bar, a comment from 'Aunt Linda' saying 'Beautiful!!! How do I share this to my wall???', and the post should be shared from a page called something like 'Sassy Quotes for Wine Lovers Over 50'. Add lens flare and a sunset gradient for no reason.
additionalInstructions: The Facebook interface should look authentic but slightly outdated. The aesthetic choices should be lovingly exaggerated but recognizable. The humor should be affectionate, not mean-spirited.

name: WATERCOLOR MOOD
message: Take a picture and transform it into a watercolor painting that captures a specific emotional mood through color temperature, brushwork intensity, and compositional choices. The subject should be rendered in transparent watercolor washes on cold-pressed paper, with the painting technique adapted to express the chosen emotional quality. Preserve the subject's identity while letting the watercolor medium carry the emotional weight through its unique properties — blooms, granulation, wet-into-wet bleeds, and the luminosity of light passing through transparent pigment to the white paper beneath.
additionalInstructions: The watercolor technique must be authentic — transparent washes, visible paper texture, proper water behavior. The emotional mood must be conveyed through color and technique choices, not just subject expression. Subject identity must be preserved.

options.text: Melancholy — cool blue-gray palette, wet-into-wet bleeds suggesting tears or rain, soft lost edges
Joy — warm golden yellows and bright oranges, energetic splatter, light-filled with white paper glowing through
Serenity — pale blue-greens and lavenders, minimal brushstrokes, vast empty space, quiet

name: MISHEARD LYRICS ILLUSTRATION
message: Take a picture and transform it into a literal illustration of a misheard song lyric (mondegreen). The subject should be depicted in a scene that visualizes what a famous song lyric sounds like when misheard — rendered completely literally and seriously as if this were the actual intended meaning. The illustration style should be earnest and well-executed (watercolor, oil painting, or detailed digital art), creating maximum contrast between the quality of the artwork and the absurdity of the literal interpretation. Include a subtle music notation border and the misheard lyric as a caption.
additionalInstructions: The misheard lyric should be a well-known mondegreen that people actually mishear. The illustration should be genuinely well-crafted — the humor comes from taking the wrong words completely seriously.

name: WEATHER PHENOMENON PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject so they appear to be made of or generating a weather phenomenon — not just standing in weather but being the weather itself. Their form should be composed of the atmospheric elements, with the phenomenon emanating from their body as if they are its source. The transformation should be beautiful and powerful, suggesting a nature deity or elemental force that has taken human shape.

options.text: Thunderstorm — body crackling with lightning, storm clouds forming from their shoulders, rain falling from their hands
Aurora borealis — form composed of shimmering curtains of green and purple light, magnetic field lines visible

Snowstorm — crystalline form, each exhale creating blizzard conditions, ice forming where they touch
Sunrise — body radiating golden light, clouds parting around them, the horizon bending to their will

Gentle manifestation — subtle, beautiful, the weather as whisper and caress
Full force — dramatic, powerful, the weather at its most awe-inspiring peak
Apocalyptic — extreme, world-changing, the weather as divine judgment

additionalInstructions: The weather phenomenon must be scientifically inspired — real atmospheric physics made magical. The subject must remain recognizable as the 'core' of the phenomenon. The overall effect should be awe-inspiring and beautiful rather than simply destructive.

name: INCREASINGLY VERBOSE
message: Take a picture and transform it into the 'Increasingly Verbose' meme format. Show the subject in a series of 4-5 panels arranged vertically, where each panel shows the same subject but with progressively more elaborate, academic, and unnecessarily complex description text beneath it. Start with a simple one-word label, then expand to a sentence, then a paragraph of purple prose, then an absurdly overwrought academic description using the most obscure vocabulary possible. Each panel's image should also become progressively more abstract or 'deep-fried' as the text becomes more verbose.
additionalInstructions: The text progression must be genuinely funny — each level should be a recognizable escalation in verbosity. The final description should be nearly incomprehensible while technically describing the same thing.

name: SCULPTURE MATERIAL STUDY
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a sculpture rendered in a specific material — capturing not just the form but the unique properties, limitations, and beauty of the chosen medium. The sculpture should show evidence of the specific techniques used to work that material, and the subject's form should be adapted to what the material naturally wants to do. The craftsmanship should be museum-quality, with the material's inherent beauty celebrated alongside the subject's recognizable form.
additionalInstructions: The material must be rendered with complete physical accuracy — correct surface properties, appropriate tool marks, realistic weight and structural behavior. The subject must be recognizable. The sculpture should feel like a real artwork in the chosen medium.

name: MEDIEVAL COMPLAINT LETTER
message: Take a picture and transform it into an illuminated medieval manuscript page containing a formal complaint letter about the subject, written in the style of a medieval scribe. The page should feature ornate decorated borders with gold leaf, illuminated capital letters, and marginalia (small illustrations in the margins) that depict the complaint being described. The text should be written in mock-medieval English ('Hear ye, hear ye, I doth lodge this most grievous complaint...') addressing a mundane modern problem as if it were a matter of great import to the kingdom. Include a wax seal and the scribe's colophon at the bottom.
additionalInstructions: The manuscript illumination should be authentically medieval in style. The mock-medieval language should be consistent and entertaining. The marginalia should add visual humor. The complaint should be about something trivially modern.

name: COMIC PANEL EMOTION
message: Take a picture and transform it into a dramatic comic book panel capturing a peak emotional moment. The subject should be rendered in bold comic art style with dynamic inking, dramatic angles, and the visual language of comics used to amplify the chosen emotion. Include appropriate comic conventions: speed lines, impact effects, emotional symbols, and dramatic lettering for any sound effects or dialogue. The panel should feel like it was torn from the climactic page of a graphic novel.
additionalInstructions: The comic art style must be professional quality — proper inking technique, dynamic composition, correct use of comic conventions. The emotion must be clearly conveyed through both the art and the comic-specific visual language. Subject must be recognizable.

name: LOADING SCREEN TIPS
message: Take a picture and transform it into a video game loading screen featuring the subject. The image should be slightly darkened with a loading bar at the bottom (stuck at 87%), and a 'helpful' gameplay tip displayed in white text. The tip should be either blindingly obvious ('Remember: You can move forward by walking forward'), passive-aggressively judgmental ('TIP: Maybe try actually reading the tutorial this time'), or completely useless for the situation depicted. Include the characteristic loading screen elements: spinning icon, percentage counter, and the slightly compressed/darkened screenshot aesthetic of real game loading screens.
additionalInstructions: The loading screen UI must look authentic to real video games. The tip should be genuinely funny — either obvious, unhelpful, or subtly insulting. Include a fake game title and studio logo.

name: FILM GRAIN ERA
message: Take a picture and transform it to look like it was shot on a specific era of photographic film — capturing not just the color science but the entire photographic culture of that period: the cameras used, the printing methods, the aesthetic preferences, and the way photographs were displayed and shared. The image should feel like an authentic artifact from the chosen era, including appropriate aging, handling marks, and presentation format.
additionalInstructions: The film characteristics must be era-accurate — correct grain structure, color science, dynamic range, and format. The presentation (print type, mounting, condition) must match the period. Subject must be recognizable across all era treatments.

name: DRAMATIC REENACTMENT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a low-budget true crime dramatic reenactment — the kind shown on daytime TV investigation shows where actors poorly recreate events. The image should have the characteristic look: slightly soft focus, overly dramatic lighting (harsh side-light with colored gels), a wig that doesn't quite fit, and the subject performing an action with maximum theatrical intensity despite the mundane nature of the scene. Include the lower-third text 'DRAMATIC REENACTMENT' in the standard true crime show font, and the slightly desaturated color grade typical of these segments.
additionalInstructions: The production quality should be recognizably 'budget' — not terrible, but clearly not a major production. The dramatic intensity should be wildly disproportionate to whatever mundane action is being depicted.

name: ARCHITECTURAL LIGHTING MOOD
message: Take a picture and transform it using a specific architectural lighting scenario — placing the subject within a space where the architecture itself shapes the light in a distinctive way. The lighting should be entirely motivated by the architectural space, with no artificial studio lighting apparent. The subject should be lit solely by how light enters and bounces within the chosen space, creating a specific mood through architecture's relationship with natural and designed light.
additionalInstructions: The lighting must be physically motivated by the architectural space — no unexplained light sources. The architecture should be convincing and specific. The mood should emerge naturally from the light quality. Subject must be clearly visible and recognizable.

name: UNHELPFUL DIAGRAM
message: Take a picture and transform it into a technical diagram or infographic that is completely unhelpful. The subject should be labeled with arrows and annotations in the style of a textbook diagram, but every label should be either blindingly obvious ('this is the face part'), wildly incorrect ('quantum flux capacitor'), or existentially unsettling ('the void stares back'). Use the clean, professional aesthetic of real educational materials — proper fonts, clean lines, numbered callouts — but with content that provides zero useful information. Include a legend, scale bar, and figure number for maximum authenticity.
additionalInstructions: The diagram format must look professionally produced and authentic. The humor comes entirely from the useless or absurd labels contrasting with the serious presentation format.

The transformation should be complete — not just the subject but the entire frame should look like a screenshot from the game, including health bars, inventory slots, dialogue boxes, or whatever interface elements are appropriate to the genre.

name: CLICKBAIT THUMBNAIL
message: Take a picture and transform it into an over-the-top YouTube clickbait thumbnail. The subject should be shown with a massively exaggerated shocked expression (mouth wide open, hands on cheeks), surrounded by red arrows pointing at nothing important, red circles highlighting random areas, and emoji reactions (😱🔥💀) scattered around. The image should be oversaturated with cranked-up contrast. Include clickbait text in bold Impact font with phrases like 'YOU WON'T BELIEVE...' or 'GONE WRONG!!!' Add a fake view count showing millions of views and a misleading title that overpromises something mundane.
additionalInstructions: The thumbnail must look authentically like real clickbait — same color grading, same text placement, same energy. The contrast between the dramatic presentation and the mundane reality should be the joke.

message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a member of a fantasy race — maintaining their recognizable features while adapting their physiology to match the chosen species. The portrait should be rendered in the style of high-quality fantasy art (concept art or book illustration quality) with appropriate costume, environment, and cultural details for the chosen race.
additionalInstructions: The fantasy race characteristics must be internally consistent and well-designed. The subject's identity must be clearly preserved — same eyes, same expression, same personality visible. message: Take a picture and transform it into a horoscope page from a magazine or app, but with brutally honest and sarcastic predictions for the subject. That was all you.' Include daily ratings for love, career, and health that are comically low.

additionalInstructions: The noir visual style must be authentic — not just desaturated but properly lit with noir conventions. The monologue text should be genuinely well-written hardboiled prose, not parody.

additionalInstructions: The contradictions should be subtle enough to require a second look. The overall composition should feel 'off' without being immediately obvious why. The handwritten notes should add another layer of unreliability.

name: NATURAL PHENOMENON PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject so they appear to be generating or embodying a natural phenomenon — their body becoming the source or manifestation of a spectacular natural event. The phenomenon should emanate from or compose their form, with the subject appearing as a force of nature given human shape. The scientific accuracy of the phenomenon should be maintained while the human form provides emotional connection to the raw power of nature.
additionalInstructions: The natural phenomenon must be scientifically accurate in its visual representation. The subject must be recognizable as the 'core' of the phenomenon. The sense of natural power should be awe-inspiring. The transformation should feel organic, not forced.

options.text: Solar eclipse — body becoming the moon passing before the sun, corona visible around their silhouette
Geyser eruption — superheated water and steam exploding upward from their form, mineral deposits
Bioluminescent tide — body dissolving into millions of glowing blue dinoflagellates in dark water
Volcanic lightning — form wreathed in ash cloud with lightning crackling within, Plinian eruption
Supercell thunderstorm — rotating mesocyclone forming from their torso, wall cloud descending
Crystal cave formation — body becoming massive selenite crystals, growing over geological time

name: SCREENPLAY FORMAT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a screenplay page with the image serving as a 'storyboard frame' in the margin. The main content should be a properly formatted screenplay page (Courier 12pt font, correct margins, scene headings in CAPS) describing the scene depicted in the image with cinematic precision. Include scene heading (INT./EXT., LOCATION, TIME), action lines describing what we see, character introductions with brief parenthetical descriptions, and dialogue if characters are present. The writing should be professional screenplay format — visual, present tense, economical prose that reads like a movie playing in your head.
additionalInstructions: The screenplay format must be industry-standard correct. The writing should be genuinely cinematic — showing not telling, with strong visual verbs and specific details. The scene should feel like it belongs in a compelling film.

name: FASHION EDITORIAL DECADE
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a high-fashion editorial photograph from a specific decade — capturing not just the clothing but the entire photographic style, makeup, hair, pose conventions, and cultural attitude of that era's fashion photography. The image should look like it was torn from the pages of Vogue, Harper's Bazaar, or a cutting-edge fashion magazine of the chosen decade. Every element should be period-authentic: the film stock/processing, the lighting style, the model's pose and expression, the set design, and the overall mood.

options.text: 1950s — Avedon elegance, New Look silhouettes, pearls, gloves, architectural poses, studio perfection
1960s — Mod revolution, Twiggy eyes, geometric cuts, pop art influence, youth quake energy
1970s — Helmut Newton drama, Studio 54 glamour, flowing fabrics, sexual liberation, warm film tones
1980s — power shoulders, excess, Patrick Demarchelier style, bold color, supermodel era begins
1990s — heroin chic minimalism, Kate Moss era, stripped back, raw, Corinne Day intimacy
2000s — digital perfection, Terry Richardson flash, Y2K futurism, glossy and provocative
High glamour — aspirational luxury, perfect lighting, untouchable beauty
Avant-garde — experimental, challenging, pushing boundaries of beauty and form
Intimate/candid — behind-the-scenes feel, natural moments, vulnerability
Narrative/cinematic — telling a story, character-driven, location-specific

additionalInstructions: The photographic style must be authentic to the decade — correct film stock look, lighting conventions, and post-processing. Fashion, hair, and makeup must be period-accurate. The subject must be recognizable while transformed into a fashion model of the era.

name: GOTHIC NOVEL FRONTISPIECE
message: Take a picture and transform it into the frontispiece illustration of a Gothic novel — the kind of engraved plate found opposite the title page in a 19th-century first edition. The image should be rendered as a steel engraving or mezzotint in the style of Victorian book illustration: fine parallel lines building tone, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, and an atmosphere of romantic dread. The subject should be placed in a Gothic setting and depicted at a moment of dramatic tension.
additionalInstructions: The engraving style must be authentic to 19th-century book illustration. The Gothic atmosphere should be genuine — romantic, mysterious, slightly threatening.

name: ANIMATION STYLE TRIBUTE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a specific animation art style — rendering the subject as if they were a character designed for that particular animation studio or show's visual language. The transformation should be complete: not just the drawing style but the color palette, line quality, proportions, and design philosophy of the chosen animation tradition. The subject should look like they naturally belong in that animated world while remaining recognizable.
additionalInstructions: The animation style must be authentically reproduced — correct proportions, proper line quality, accurate color palette, and design philosophy. The subject must be recognizable despite the stylistic transformation. The character should look like they belong in that animated world.

options.text: Studio Ghibli — soft watercolor backgrounds, detailed naturalistic style, Miyazaki character design, gentle
Cartoon Network 2000s — bold outlines, geometric shapes, limited palette, energetic and graphic
Disney Renaissance — expressive eyes, flowing lines, musical energy, Broadway-influenced drama
Vintage Fleischer — rubber hose limbs, surreal backgrounds, jazz-age energy, black and white with gray
Anime shonen — dynamic poses, speed lines, detailed eyes, spiky hair, battle-ready intensity
Stop-motion Laika — slightly imperfect, visible texture, handcrafted quality, dark whimsy
French animation (Sylvain Chomet) — exaggerated proportions, muted palette, melancholic beauty, detailed backgrounds

name: RECIPE AS LOVE LETTER
message: Take a picture and transform it into a handwritten recipe card that doubles as a love letter. The image should show a vintage-style recipe card (stained with use, slightly yellowed) where the recipe instructions are written in a way that reveals deep affection — each cooking instruction is also a metaphor for love ('Fold gently, the way you fold me into your arms on Sunday mornings'). The subject of the image should be incorporated as either the dish being described or the person the recipe is written for. Include ingredient lists with emotional annotations, temperature settings described as feelings, and timing instructions measured in memories.
additionalInstructions: The recipe must be a real, followable recipe with actual cooking instructions. The love letter layer should be woven naturally into the cooking language, not forced. The card should look genuinely used and treasured.

name: COCKTAIL NAPKIN SKETCH
message: Take a picture and transform it into a cocktail napkin sketch — the kind of brilliant, spontaneous drawing done on a bar napkin during a conversation. The subject should be rendered in quick, confident pen strokes on a slightly crumpled white cocktail napkin, with the characteristic qualities: slightly bleeding ink where the napkin absorbed it, a ring stain from a glass partially overlapping the drawing, the small square format of a standard napkin, and the energetic economy of a sketch done in minutes with no erasing possible. The drawing should feel like a moment of inspiration captured — loose but accurate, casual but skilled. Include the napkin's embossed logo or pattern visible beneath the ink.
additionalInstructions: The napkin texture must be visible — slightly absorbent, causing ink to bleed slightly. The sketch must feel spontaneous and confident — no hesitation marks. The cocktail ring stain adds authenticity. The subject must be recognizable from minimal, confident lines. The small format should feel intimate.

options.text: Ballpoint pen — blue ink, slightly scratchy, varying pressure creating line weight, casual
Fine-tip marker — black, consistent line weight, slightly bleeding into napkin fibers, graphic
Fountain pen — rich black ink, expressive line variation, occasional ink pooling, elegant
Pencil stub — soft graphite, smudged slightly, erasure attempts visible, working sketch
Multiple pens — different colors grabbed from the bar, layered sketch, colorful and spontaneous

name: FIELD JOURNAL ENTRY
message: Take a picture and transform it into a page from a naturalist's field journal — the kind kept by Victorian-era explorers and scientists. The page should combine detailed observational illustration (precise watercolor and ink rendering of the subject as if it were a newly discovered specimen) with handwritten field notes in a cramped but elegant hand. Include measurements, behavioral observations, habitat notes, date and location stamps, and small marginal sketches of details. The tone should be that of a passionate scientist encountering something remarkable for the first time — precise yet full of wonder.
additionalInstructions: The scientific illustration should be precise and beautiful. The handwritten notes should feel authentic — including crossed-out words, ink blots, and margin additions. The overall page should feel like a genuine historical document.

name: FOOD PHOTOGRAPHY STYLE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a professional food photography shot — but with the subject reimagined AS a food item being photographed for a cookbook, menu, or food magazine. The subject should be 'plated' and styled with the obsessive attention to detail of professional food photography: perfect garnish placement, strategic sauce drizzles, steam or condensation added for freshness, and the specific lighting and composition conventions of food photography. The styling should make the subject appear genuinely appetizing through the visual language of food advertising.
additionalInstructions: The food photography conventions must be authentic — correct lighting angles, proper styling techniques, realistic food photography composition. The subject should be treated with the same reverence as a hero dish. The overall image should look like it belongs in a high-end food publication.

options.text: Overhead flat lay — shot directly from above, styled on a textured surface with scattered ingredients and props
Hero shot 45-degree — classic food angle, shallow depth of field, backlit steam, dramatic
Action pour/drizzle — frozen motion of sauce or liquid being poured, dynamic and appetizing
Rustic lifestyle — natural light, wooden surfaces, linen napkins, imperfect beauty, homestyle
Dark and moody — black background, dramatic side light, rich colors emerging from shadow, editorial
Bright and clean — white background, even lighting, minimal props, commercial product-shot style

name: SOCIAL MEDIA BIO AS NOVEL
message: Take a picture and transform it into a book cover for a literary novel whose title and synopsis are derived from the subject's imagined social media bio. The cover should be designed in the style of contemporary literary fiction (minimalist design, clever typography, muted color palette, a single evocative image). The title should be something a millennial would use as their Instagram bio turned into a novel title. Include back cover blurbs from fake literary critics, a barcode, publisher logo, and a synopsis that treats mundane life details as profound literary themes. The overall design should look like it belongs on a 'Staff Picks' shelf at an independent bookstore.
additionalInstructions: The book cover design must look professionally published. The title and synopsis should be genuinely clever — finding the literary in the everyday. The critic blurbs should sound authentically pretentious.

name: MAP STYLE PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject's portrait into a specific cartographic style — their features rendered using the visual language and conventions of a particular type of map. The portrait should be readable both as a face and as a functional map, with proper cartographic elements (legend, scale, compass rose) included. The map conventions should be followed precisely while the subject's likeness emerges from the cartographic elements.
additionalInstructions: The cartographic style must be authentic — correct conventions, proper symbols, realistic map elements. The subject must be recognizable through the map features. Both readings (portrait and map) should work simultaneously. Include proper cartographic notation.

options.text: Topographic contour — USGS-style brown contour lines following facial terrain, elevation numbers at peaks
Transit/subway map — simplified geometric lines in bold colors, station dots at feature points, route names
Nautical chart — depth soundings, shipping lanes, lighthouse symbols, blue water areas, compass rose
Road atlas — highways following major features, town names at key points, distance markers, grid reference
Geological survey — rock type colors, fault lines, mineral deposits marked, cross-section inset
Fantasy adventure map — hand-drawn style, 'Here Be Dragons,' quest path marked, treasure X

name: VILLANELLE PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into an artistic portrait overlaid with a villanelle poem about the subject. The portrait should be rendered in a Pre-Raphaelite style — rich colors, detailed naturalism, symbolic elements woven into the composition. The villanelle (19-line poem with two repeating refrains in the pattern ABA ABA ABA ABA ABA ABAA) should be overlaid in elegant typography that follows the curves of the composition. The poem's refrains should capture something essential about the subject — a defining quality or moment that gains power through repetition.
additionalInstructions: The villanelle must follow the correct form — 19 lines, five tercets and a quatrain, with proper refrain repetition. The portrait style should be genuinely Pre-Raphaelite. The poem and image should enhance each other.

name: TAROT CARD DESIGN
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a tarot card — a richly symbolic illustration following the traditions of tarot art. The subject should be depicted as the central figure of the card, surrounded by the traditional symbolic elements associated with the chosen card's meaning. The design should include the card name, number, and suit (for minor arcana) in appropriate typography. The border should be ornate and mystical. The illustration should be rich with hidden symbolism that rewards close inspection.

options.text: The Magician (I) — one hand raised to heaven, one pointing to earth, infinity symbol, four suit symbols on table
The High Priestess (II) — seated between pillars, crescent moon, scroll of wisdom, veil of mystery
The Emperor (IV) — throne of authority, ram symbols, orb and scepter, mountain backdrop
The Star (XVII) — kneeling by water, pouring from two vessels, eight-pointed star above, hope and renewal
The World (XXI) — dancing within a wreath, four creatures in corners, completion and achievement
The Tower (XVI) — lightning strike, falling figures, crown toppling, sudden revelation
The Moon (XVIII) — two towers, howling creatures, path between, illusion and intuition
Rider-Waite traditional — classic symbolic illustration, flat colors, medieval-inspired
Art Nouveau — Mucha-inspired flowing lines, decorative borders, organic forms
Dark/Gothic — dramatic shadows, occult symbolism, rich jewel tones, mysterious
Modern minimalist — clean lines, limited palette, geometric interpretation of symbols

additionalInstructions: The tarot symbolism must be accurate to traditional meanings. The card layout must follow standard tarot card proportions and formatting. The subject must be recognizable as the central figure. Hidden symbolic details should reward close inspection.

name: EPISTOLARY PHOTOGRAPH
message: Take a picture and transform it into a vintage photograph tucked into a handwritten letter — as if discovered in an old trunk or between the pages of a book. The photograph should be rendered as a faded, slightly sepia-toned print with white borders and a date stamp. The letter visible around and behind the photo should be written in fountain pen on aged paper, referencing the moment captured in the photograph with intimate detail and emotion. Include the envelope, a pressed flower, and perhaps a second partially-visible photo. The letter should hint at a larger story — love, loss, distance, or reunion.
additionalInstructions: The aging effects should be subtle and realistic. The letter text should be genuinely moving and hint at a compelling story. The overall composition should feel like a discovered artifact with emotional weight.

name: LIGHT PAINTING PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a light painting photograph — the subject's portrait created by moving light sources during a long exposure in complete darkness. The image should show the characteristic qualities of light painting: smooth, flowing lines of light against absolute black, the way different light sources create different qualities (LED vs. sparkler vs. fiber optic), and the ethereal quality of light frozen in time.
