The subject's features should be outlined or filled with light trails, with the darkness between strokes creating the shadows and form.
additionalInstructions: The light painting must follow real long-exposure physics — smooth continuous lines, proper light falloff, realistic color from different light sources. The absolute darkness between light trails is essential. The subject must be recognizable from the light-painted outlines. The technique should feel like genuine light painting, not digital drawing.

options.text: Single color outline — one continuous LED line tracing the subject's contours, minimal and elegant
Multi-color fill — different colored lights filling different areas, painterly and vibrant
Steel wool sparks — spinning burning steel wool creating circular spark showers around the subject
Fiber optic brush — soft, diffused strokes of light creating a painterly, impressionistic portrait
Flashlight selective — subject partially illuminated by brief flashlight bursts during long exposure, mysterious

name: CONCRETE POETRY SHAPE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a concrete (shape) poem where the text forms the visual outline and details of the subject. The entire image should be constructed from words and letters — no traditional illustration, only typography arranged to create the visual form. The words used should be thematically related to the subject, creating meaning through both their content and their spatial arrangement. Vary font sizes, weights, and densities to create tonal values — dense small text for dark areas, sparse large text for highlights. The poem should be readable both as text and as image simultaneously.
additionalInstructions: The text must be legible and meaningful — not just random letters filling space. The visual form must be clearly recognizable as the subject. The interplay between verbal and visual meaning should create something greater than either alone.

name: BOOK GENRE COVER
message: Take a picture and transform it into a book cover design — the subject featured as the protagonist on a genre fiction cover. The design should follow the specific visual conventions of the chosen genre: appropriate typography, color palette, composition, and imagery that immediately signals to readers what kind of book this is. The cover should look professionally designed and publishable, with all standard elements: title, author name, tagline, and publisher logo.
additionalInstructions: The book cover must follow real genre conventions — readers should immediately identify the genre from the design. Typography must be genre-appropriate. The subject must be featured as the protagonist. The overall design must look professionally publishable.

options.text: Epic fantasy — embossed metallic title, cloaked figure, map elements, dark atmospheric background
Thriller/mystery — high contrast, partially hidden face, bold red title, urban noir atmosphere
Romance — soft focus, warm colors, intimate pose, script font title, emotional connection
Science fiction — sleek typography, technological elements, vast scale, blue/silver palette
Literary fiction — minimalist design, single symbolic object, elegant serif title, white space
Horror — dark palette, unsettling imagery, dripping or distressed title font, dread
Young adult — bold colorful design, character-focused, dynamic pose, contemporary typography

name: DELETED SCENE STORYBOARD
message: Take a picture and transform it into a storyboard for a 'deleted scene' — a sequence that was supposedly cut from a famous film for being too strange, too revealing, or too expensive to produce. The storyboard should be in professional format: rectangular panels with arrows indicating camera movement, brief action descriptions below each frame, and technical notes (CRANE UP, SMASH CUT, SFX: thunder). The subject should be integrated into a scene that feels like it could belong in a real film but explains something that was always a plot hole or unanswered question. Include the director's handwritten margin notes explaining why the scene was cut.
additionalInstructions: The storyboard format must be professional and authentic. The 'deleted scene' should feel genuinely plausible — like it could have existed. The director's notes should add humor or insight.

name: CULTURAL TEXTILE PATTERN
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a traditional textile pattern from a specific cultural tradition — their portrait woven, printed, or embroidered into the fabric using the authentic techniques, motifs, and color palettes of that textile tradition. The portrait should be integrated into the larger pattern repeat, surrounded by traditional motifs and borders. The textile should show the physical qualities of the actual fabric: thread texture, weave structure, and the way the pattern is constructed through the specific technique.
additionalInstructions: The textile tradition must be authentically represented — correct techniques, proper motifs, accurate color palettes, and realistic fabric texture. The subject must be recognizable within the pattern. The cultural context must be respectful and well-researched.

options.text: Persian carpet — intricate knotted wool, medallion composition, rich reds and blues, floral borders
Kente cloth — bold geometric strips, symbolic color combinations, woven silk and cotton, Ashanti tradition
Japanese shibori — indigo resist-dyed patterns, tied and bound fabric creating organic shapes
Navajo weaving — geometric patterns, natural wool colors, spirit line, horizontal loom texture
Indian block print — hand-stamped repeated motifs, natural dyes, cotton fabric, Rajasthani tradition
Scottish tartan — precise intersecting colored stripes, wool twill weave, clan-specific pattern

name: PROPHECY SCROLL
message: Take a picture and transform it into an ancient prophecy scroll that foretells the subject's destiny. The scroll should appear as aged parchment — tea-stained, edges burned or torn, rolled at top and bottom with wooden dowels. The prophecy text should be written in an archaic calligraphic hand with illuminated details, using the deliberately ambiguous and metaphorical language of prophecy ('When the shadow of the iron bird falls upon the mountain's crown, the one who bears the mark of three shall rise...'). Include mystical diagrams, astrological charts, and symbolic illustrations that relate to the subject. The prophecy should be specific enough to clearly reference the subject but vague enough to feel authentically prophetic.
additionalInstructions: The scroll aging must look realistic. The prophecy language should be genuinely evocative and ambiguous. The mystical diagrams should look like real occult or astrological notation. The subject should be clearly referenced through symbolic language.

name: CHILDREN'S BOOK SPREAD
message: Take a picture and transform it into a double-page spread from a children's picture book. The illustration should be warm, inviting, and slightly whimsical — in the style of beloved children's book illustrators (think Oliver Jeffers, Jon Klassen, or Beatrix Potter). The subject should be depicted as a character in a gentle story, with the illustration capturing a quiet, emotionally resonant moment. Include picture book text in a friendly font — simple, rhythmic prose or gentle rhyme that a parent would enjoy reading aloud. The text and image should work together to tell more than either could alone. Leave space for the child's imagination.
additionalInstructions: The illustration style should be genuinely appealing to children — warm, safe, with hidden details to discover. The text should be simple but not simplistic. The emotional tone should be gentle and affirming.

name: BIOLUMINESCENT DEEP SEA
message: Take a picture and transform the subject as if they exist in the deep ocean's midnight zone, adapted for life in complete darkness. Their features should emit soft bioluminescent light — glowing patterns along their contours like deep-sea creatures (anglerfish lures, jellyfish pulses, dinoflagellate sparkles). The background should be the absolute black of the deep ocean with only the subject's own light illuminating the scene. Translucent and iridescent qualities should replace opaque skin. The overall effect should be hauntingly beautiful — life creating its own light in infinite darkness.
additionalInstructions: The bioluminescence should be the ONLY light source — no external lighting. The deep ocean darkness must be absolute. The subject must remain recognizable through their glowing features. Colors should be limited to what bioluminescence actually produces: blues, greens, and occasional reds.

name: MOVIE GENRE POSTER
message: Take a picture and transform it into a movie poster — a professional theatrical one-sheet that sells the subject as the star of a film. The poster should follow the specific visual conventions of the chosen genre, with appropriate typography, color palette, composition, and tagline. Include all standard movie poster elements: title, star name, director credit, release date, studio logos, and billing block at the bottom. The subject should be posed and lit according to genre conventions.

options.text: Action/thriller — dramatic lighting, weapon or vehicle, explosion hints, intense expression
Romantic comedy — warm colors, playful pose, city skyline, charming smile
Horror — dark palette, ominous shadow, fear in eyes, something lurking
Science fiction — blue/teal palette, futuristic elements, vast scale, wonder
Period drama — painterly quality, costume detail, atmospheric landscape, dignity
Indie/arthouse — minimalist design, unusual composition, muted palette, contemplative
Classic Hollywood (1950s-60s) — painted illustration, bold colors, dramatic composition
New Hollywood (1970s) — photographic, gritty, innovative typography, auteur-driven
Blockbuster era (1980s-90s) — floating heads, blue/orange palette, Photoshop compositing
Modern minimalist — negative space, single striking image, restrained typography
International/Criterion — artistic interpretation, symbolic imagery, design-forward

additionalInstructions: The poster must look professionally designed and printable. Genre conventions must be followed precisely. The billing block must look authentic (even if names are fictional). The subject must be the clear star of the film. The tagline should be genre-appropriate and compelling.

name: LIBRARY OF BABEL
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into an inhabitant of Borges' Library of Babel — an infinite library containing every possible combination of letters ever written or that could be written. The subject should be shown within the hexagonal galleries, surrounded by endless identical bookshelves stretching into infinity in all directions. The architecture should follow Borges' description precisely: hexagonal rooms, spiral staircases connecting levels, a ventilation shaft in the center of each hexagon. The subject should appear small against the incomprehensible vastness, perhaps holding one of the library's books — most containing only gibberish, but one, perhaps, containing the story of their life.
additionalInstructions: The infinite repetition of the library must be conveyed through perspective. The hexagonal geometry must be precise. The subject should appear contemplative and slightly overwhelmed by the infinite knowledge surrounding them.

name: OVERGROWN RECLAMATION
message: Take a picture and transform the subject as if decades have passed and nature has begun reclaiming them. Vines grow through and around their form, moss covers surfaces, small trees sprout from crevices, and flowers bloom in unexpected places. The subject should appear as a statue or structure that has been abandoned to the forest — still recognizable but being slowly, beautifully consumed by plant life. Birds nest in their hair, mushrooms grow from shadows, and roots crack through their base. The overall feeling should be peaceful rather than post-apocalyptic — nature's patient, gentle victory over human form.
additionalInstructions: The plant growth must follow realistic patterns — moss on north-facing surfaces, vines climbing toward light, roots following gravity. The subject must remain clearly identifiable beneath the growth. The mood should be serene, not threatening.

name: QUANTUM SUPERPOSITION
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a visual representation of quantum superposition — existing in multiple states simultaneously until observed. The subject should appear in several overlapping translucent versions of themselves, each in a slightly different position, expression, or state, all occupying the same space. The overlapping forms should create interference patterns where they intersect, like light waves combining. Some versions should be more solid (more probable states) while others are barely visible (less probable). Include subtle visual references to quantum mechanics: probability clouds, wave function patterns, and the suggestion that observation is collapsing these possibilities into one.
additionalInstructions: The multiple states should feel simultaneous, not sequential. The interference patterns where versions overlap should be visually interesting. The subject must be recognizable in at least the most prominent version.

name: CARTOGRAPHIC SELF
message: Take a picture and transform the subject's body into a detailed topographic map — their form becoming a landscape to be explored and charted. Contour lines follow the curves of their body, elevation markers indicate high points, rivers flow along natural creases, forests grow in shadowed areas, and cities cluster at intersections. The map should be drawn in the style of vintage cartography with compass roses, scale bars, decorative cartouches, and sea monsters in the margins. Place names should be personal and meaningful — 'The Valley of Childhood Memories,' 'Mount Ambition,' 'The Sea of Doubt.' The subject's form should be clearly readable as both a person and a complete mapped territory.
additionalInstructions: The cartographic style must be authentic to vintage mapmaking. The place names should feel personal and poetic. The topographic contours must follow the actual form of the subject's body. Include a proper legend and scale.

name: STAINED GLASS CATHEDRAL
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a stained glass window — not just flat colored glass, but a full cathedral window with the subject as the central figure, backlit by divine light streaming through. The lead came lines should follow the subject's contours, dividing the image into jewel-toned glass segments. Each piece of glass should show the characteristic texture of real stained glass: slight bubbles, color variations within single pieces, and the way light passes differently through thick and thin areas. The surrounding window should include Gothic tracery, decorative borders, and symbolic elements appropriate to the subject. The light streaming through should cast colored reflections.
additionalInstructions: The lead came lines must follow logical structural patterns. Glass colors should be rich and saturated. The backlighting effect must be convincing — light passing THROUGH the glass. Gothic architectural framing should be accurate.

name: CLOCKWORK INTERIOR
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a cross-section view revealing an intricate clockwork interior. The outer surface should appear partially opened or cut away (like an anatomical illustration) to reveal that inside, the subject is entirely composed of brass gears, springs, escapements, balance wheels, and tiny mechanical components all working in precise harmony. Each visible mechanism should be detailed and functional-looking — not random gears but purposeful mechanical systems that suggest specific functions (a heart made of a mainspring, lungs as bellows, eyes as camera obscura mechanisms). The craftsmanship should suggest a master horologist's finest work.
additionalInstructions: The mechanical components must look functional and purposeful, not decorative. The cross-section should follow anatomical logic — mechanisms in places that make metaphorical sense. Brass, copper, and steel materials should be rendered with realistic metallic qualities.

name: CONSTELLATION FORM
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a constellation in the night sky. The subject's key features and outline should be defined by bright stars of varying magnitudes, connected by the traditional constellation line patterns. The background should be a deep, realistic night sky filled with the Milky Way, nebulae, and countless dimmer stars. Include a constellation chart overlay showing the traditional astronomical notation: Greek letter star designations (α, β, γ), magnitude indicators, and the constellation boundary lines. Add a mythological illustration overlay (in the style of classical star atlases like Uranometria) showing the subject's form drawn over the star pattern.
additionalInstructions: The night sky must be astronomically realistic. The constellation pattern should be simple enough to be recognizable (like real constellations) while clearly suggesting the subject's form. Include proper astronomical notation.

name: ORIGAMI TRANSFORMATION
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a complex origami sculpture — folded from a single sheet of paper with no cuts or glue. The form should clearly be the subject but constructed entirely through precise geometric folds. Show the paper's surface with visible fold lines, the slight translucency where paper is thinnest at fold points, and the mathematical precision of origami geometry. The paper should be a single color (or traditional origami paper with color on one side, white on the other) so that the interplay of colored and white surfaces creates additional visual interest. Light should catch the faceted surfaces differently, creating natural shading through geometry alone.
additionalInstructions: The folds must look physically possible from a single sheet. The geometric faceting should create recognizable form through angular approximation. Paper texture and translucency at fold points should be visible.

name: TERRARIUM WORLD
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a living terrarium — contained within a glass vessel (bell jar, geometric terrarium, or glass sphere) with an entire miniature ecosystem growing around and through them. The subject should be miniaturized and integrated into the terrarium landscape: tiny ferns unfurling around their feet, moss covering their lower portions, condensation on the glass near their breath, and small insects or amphibians sharing their space. The glass container should show realistic reflections and the slight green tint of thick glass. The ecosystem should be self-contained and thriving — a perfect tiny world.
additionalInstructions: The glass container must show realistic optical properties — reflections, refraction, condensation. The miniature ecosystem must be botanically plausible. The subject should appear peaceful and integrated into their tiny world, not trapped.

name: COCKTAIL MENU PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a signature cocktail — illustrated on a craft cocktail bar menu. The subject's personality, colors, and essence should be translated into a drink recipe with an illustrated presentation. The menu design should be appropriate to the bar's style, with the cocktail named after or inspired by the subject. Include ingredients list, preparation method, glassware illustration, and garnish details.

options.text: Speakeasy — art deco design, gold foil on dark paper, prohibition-era elegance
Tiki bar — tropical illustration, bamboo borders, exotic ingredients, fun and colorful
Modern craft — minimalist design, botanical illustrations, clean typography, artisanal
Dive bar — hand-written chalkboard, casual, irreverent, cheap and cheerful
Molecular mixology — scientific diagram style, lab equipment, precise measurements
Whiskey/bourbon — warm amber tones, oak and smoke, classic and bold
Gin — botanical, floral, juniper, crisp and complex
Rum — tropical, caramel, spice, adventurous and warm
Mezcal/tequila — smoky, agave, earthy, mysterious and complex
Vodka — clean, versatile, modern, letting other flavors shine

additionalInstructions: The cocktail recipe must be a plausible, well-balanced drink. The menu design must be authentic to the chosen bar style. The connection between the subject and the cocktail should be creative and clear. Include proper cocktail-making terminology.

name: PRISMATIC LIGHT BEING
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a being made entirely of refracted light — as if a prism has split white light into its component wavelengths and those wavelengths have taken human form. The subject should appear to be composed of pure spectral color: red at the extremities fading through orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet toward the center. Their form should have the quality of light itself — slightly transparent, casting rainbow caustics on surrounding surfaces, and appearing to glow from within. Edges should show chromatic aberration and light diffraction patterns. The background should be dark to make the light-form maximally visible.
additionalInstructions: The spectral colors must follow the correct order of the visible spectrum. The light quality must feel genuine — not just colored but actually luminous. The subject's form and identity must be clearly readable through the light effects.

name: FOSSIL IMPRESSION
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a fossil impression in sedimentary rock — as if they were preserved millions of years ago and just split open from a rock nodule. The subject should appear as a detailed impression in stone, showing the characteristic qualities of real fossils: compression into two dimensions, preservation of fine surface detail (skin texture, hair strands, fabric weave), the surrounding rock matrix with its layers and mineral inclusions, and the slight distortion that comes from geological pressure over millions of years. The stone should be split along a natural bedding plane, with the subject's impression in one half and the counter-impression suggested in the other.
additionalInstructions: The geological context must be realistic — proper sedimentary layering, mineral staining, and preservation quality. The fossil should look scientifically plausible. Include a scale bar and specimen number as a museum would.

name: NEON WIREFRAME
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a glowing neon wireframe — the aesthetic of 1980s computer graphics and Tron-era digital visualization. The subject should be reduced to their essential geometric form, outlined in bright neon lines (cyan, magenta, electric blue) against a pure black void. The wireframe should be detailed enough to be clearly recognizable but simplified to polygonal geometry. Add a reflective grid plane beneath (the classic '80s digital landscape grid receding to a horizon line). Include scan lines, slight glow bloom on the neon edges, and the suggestion of vector display phosphor persistence. No solid surfaces — only luminous edges defining form.
additionalInstructions: Only wireframe edges should be visible — no filled polygons or solid surfaces. The neon glow must feel like actual light emission. The retro-digital aesthetic should be authentic to early '80s computer graphics. Subject must be clearly recognizable from the wireframe alone.

name: PUPPET STRINGS
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a life-sized marionette puppet — with visible joints, strings, and the wooden control cross (marionette bar) visible above them. The subject should retain their real appearance but with subtle puppet qualities: slightly visible joint lines at knees, elbows, and jaw; the characteristic slight stiffness of puppet posture; and thin strings connecting their limbs to the control bar above. The strings should be taut and clearly functional. The image should raise the question of who is controlling the puppet — the control bar should extend upward out of frame, into darkness or clouds, with no puppeteer visible. The mood should be contemplative rather than sinister.
additionalInstructions: The puppet qualities should be subtle — this is a realistic figure with puppet elements, not a wooden toy. The strings must be physically convincing. The mood should be philosophical, not horror. Subject identity must be fully preserved.

name: CORAL REEF BODY
message: Take a picture and transform the subject so they appear to be a living coral reef formation — their body structure providing the substrate for an entire marine ecosystem. Hard and soft corals grow from their surfaces in vibrant colors (electric blues, hot pinks, deep purples, bright yellows), small tropical fish swim through spaces in their form, sea anemones wave from crevices, and the clear tropical water filters blue-green light across everything. The subject's basic form should be recognizable as the 'reef structure' but completely colonized by marine life. The underwater lighting should be authentic — dappled from surface waves above, with color absorption making reds disappear at depth.
additionalInstructions: The marine life must be biologically accurate — real species of coral, fish, and invertebrates. Underwater lighting physics must be correct. The subject's form should be clearly readable beneath the reef growth.

name: GOLDEN HOUR PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a golden hour portrait — shot in the last 30 minutes before sunset when the sun is low on the horizon and light becomes warm, soft, and directional. The light should be coming from a low angle, creating long shadows and wrapping warmly around the subject's features. Skin should glow with warm amber tones. The background should show the characteristic golden hour qualities: backlit edges creating rim light on hair and shoulders, lens flare from shooting toward the sun, and the overall warm color temperature (around 3000K) that makes everything look romantic and cinematic. Shadows should be soft and filled with reflected warm light from the environment.
additionalInstructions: The lighting direction must be consistent and low-angle. The warmth should feel natural, not filtered. Skin tones should be flattered by the warm light. The overall mood should be romantic and cinematic.

name: DUTCH ANGLE TENSION
message: Take a picture and transform it using a dramatic Dutch angle (tilted camera) composition to create visual tension and unease. The horizon line should be tilted 15-30 degrees, making the world feel off-kilter and unstable. Combine with noir-influenced lighting: strong side light creating deep shadows, slightly desaturated color palette, and high contrast. The subject should be positioned using the resulting diagonal lines to create dynamic visual flow. The Dutch angle should feel intentional and cinematic (like Carol Reed's The Third Man or a Batman film) rather than accidental. Include environmental elements that emphasize the tilt — vertical lines that are now diagonal, creating maximum visual instability.
additionalInstructions: The tilt must be deliberate and dramatic — not subtle. Lighting should enhance the sense of unease. The composition should use the diagonal lines created by the tilt to guide the eye. Subject should remain the clear focal point.

name: RING FLASH FASHION
message: Take a picture and transform it using ring flash lighting — the distinctive on-axis flash that creates the signature fashion photography look. The lighting should show the telltale ring flash characteristics: nearly shadowless frontal illumination, the distinctive circular catchlight in the eyes (a ring rather than a point), a thin hard shadow outline visible just behind the subject on the background, and the slight falloff of light at the edges of frame. Colors should be punchy and saturated (ring flash tends to boost saturation). The overall aesthetic should be high-fashion editorial — bold, graphic, and slightly confrontational. The background should be simple to emphasize the distinctive lighting quality.
additionalInstructions: The ring-shaped catchlight in the eyes is essential and must be visible. The shadow halo behind the subject must be present. The flat, frontal quality of ring flash must be authentic. The mood should be fashion-editorial.

name: CROSS-PROCESSED SLIDE FILM
message: Take a picture and transform it to look like cross-processed slide film (E-6 film processed in C-41 chemistry). This creates the distinctive cross-processing look: extreme color shifts (typically strong cyan/blue shadows and yellow/green highlights), increased contrast with crushed shadows, color casts that shift across the tonal range, and unpredictable saturation boosts. The effect should feel authentically chemical — not a simple color filter but the complex, non-linear color response of actual cross-processing where different layers of the film respond differently to the wrong chemistry. Include slight film base color and sprocket hole edges for authenticity.
additionalInstructions: The color shifts must feel chemical and non-linear — different in shadows vs. highlights. The effect should be strong but not so extreme that the subject is unrecognizable. Include analog film artifacts for authenticity.

name: MUSEUM EXHIBIT DISPLAY
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a museum exhibit — displayed behind glass with professional museum lighting, informational placards, and curatorial context. The subject should appear as an artifact or specimen worthy of preservation and study, presented with the reverence and scholarly attention of a world-class museum. The exhibit design should be appropriate to the chosen museum type.

options.text: Natural history — specimen display, taxonomic classification, habitat diorama context
Art museum — gallery wall, gilt frame, artist placard, critical analysis text
Science/technology — interactive display, cross-section model, timeline context
History/anthropology — cultural context, period artifacts alongside, historical narrative
Curiosity cabinet (Wunderkammer) — eclectic display, handwritten labels, wonder and mystery
Pristine/newly acquired — perfect condition, fresh discovery excitement, 'New Acquisition' banner
Ancient/weathered — showing age beautifully, conservation notes, centuries of history
Under restoration — partially cleaned, conservator's tools nearby, before/after comparison

additionalInstructions: The museum display must look professionally curated — correct lighting angles, proper display materials, authentic placard formatting. The informational text should be educational and well-written. The subject must be presented with genuine curatorial respect and scholarly interest.

name: REMBRANDT LIGHTING PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it using Rembrandt lighting — the classic portrait lighting pattern named after the Dutch master painter. Position the key light high and to one side (approximately 45 degrees) so it creates the signature small triangle of light on the shadow side of the face, just below the eye. The shadow side should be predominantly dark with this single triangle of illumination as the defining characteristic. The lighting ratio should be dramatic (at least 4:1) creating deep, rich shadows with minimal fill. The background should be dark, falling off to near-black, focusing all attention on the subject's face emerging from shadow. The mood should be contemplative and dignified.
additionalInstructions: The triangle of light on the cheek is the essential element — it must be clearly visible and properly positioned (below the eye, above the jawline, not touching the nose shadow). The overall mood should be painterly and dignified.

name: FREELENSING TILT
message: Take a picture and transform it using the freelensing technique — where the lens is detached from the camera body and held at an angle, creating a selective focus plane that cuts diagonally across the image. Only a thin slice of the image should be in sharp focus, with everything else dissolving into extreme blur. Light leaks should enter through the gap between lens and body, creating warm flares and haze. The focus plane should cut across the subject at an unexpected angle (not parallel to the sensor), creating the distinctive tilt-shift-like effect but more organic and unpredictable. The overall mood should be dreamy and intimate.
additionalInstructions: The focus plane must be clearly tilted — not just shallow DOF but a diagonal plane of focus. Light leaks should be warm and organic. The in-focus area should include the most important part of the subject. The effect should feel handmade and imperfect.

name: LARGE FORMAT VIEW CAMERA
message: Take a picture and transform it into a large format (4x5 or 8x10) view camera photograph. Show the distinctive qualities of large format: extraordinary resolution and detail throughout the entire frame, the ability to control the plane of focus through camera movements (tilt/shift), virtually grainless smooth tonality, and the unique perspective control that eliminates converging lines. The image should have the contemplative, precise quality of photographers like Ansel Adams or Edward Weston — every element in the frame considered and placed with intention. The tonal range should be extraordinary, from deep textured shadows to bright detailed highlights, with smooth gradation between.
additionalInstructions: The resolution and detail should be extraordinary — suggesting a very large negative. The depth of field should be extensive (using tilts). The overall quality should feel contemplative and precise. Include the 4:5 aspect ratio.

name: DAGUERREOTYPE REVIVAL
message: Take a picture and transform it into a daguerreotype — the first commercially successful photographic process from 1839. The image should appear on a mirror-like silver surface that shifts between positive and negative depending on viewing angle. Show the characteristic daguerreotype qualities: extraordinary sharpness and detail (each grain of silver is microscopic), the mirror-like reflective surface, slight hand-coloring on cheeks and jewelry (as was common practice), and the image contained within a decorative brass mat and leather case. The exposure should suggest the long sitting times of the era — a formal, composed pose with a slight softness from micro-movement during the multi-second exposure.
additionalInstructions: The mirror-like surface quality is essential — the image should appear to float on polished silver. The brass mat and case framing should be authentic to the 1840s-1860s period. Hand-coloring should be subtle and period-appropriate.

name: MULTIPLE EXPOSURE IN-CAMERA
message: Take a picture and transform it into an in-camera multiple exposure — two or three exposures combined on a single frame of film without any digital compositing. The overlapping images should interact through additive light (bright areas of one exposure dominate, dark areas allow the other exposure to show through). The subject should appear in one exposure while a complementary image (landscape, texture, architecture, or abstract pattern) occupies the other, creating a dreamlike fusion where both images coexist in the same frame. The combination should feel intentional and poetic — not random overlap but meaningful visual dialogue between the layers.
additionalInstructions: The exposure combination must follow real photographic physics — light areas dominate, dark areas reveal underlying exposures. The two images should create meaningful visual poetry together. The effect should feel analog, not digitally composited.

name: ZONE SYSTEM PERFECTION
message: Take a picture and transform it into a perfect Zone System black and white photograph — the technical approach developed by Ansel Adams and Fred Archer for precise tonal control. The image should demonstrate mastery of all 11 zones: from Zone 0 (pure black) through Zone V (middle gray) to Zone X (pure white), with every zone represented and perfectly placed. The most important subject values should fall on Zone V-VI, with textured shadows in Zone III and textured highlights in Zone VII. The print should appear on silver gelatin fiber paper with the full tonal range that only careful exposure and development control can achieve. Every tone should feel intentional and precisely placed.
additionalInstructions: The tonal range must be complete and precisely controlled — this is technical perfection in black and white. The print quality should suggest fiber-based silver gelatin paper. Every tonal value should feel deliberate.

name: PETZVAL LENS SWIRL
message: Take a picture and transform it using the distinctive optical characteristics of a Petzval lens — the 1840 lens design famous for its unique rendering. The center of the image should be tack-sharp with beautiful contrast, while the background bokeh swirls in a distinctive circular pattern around the subject (the famous 'Petzval swirl'). This swirling bokeh is caused by the lens's strong field curvature and should create a sense of motion and energy in the out-of-focus areas while the subject remains perfectly still and sharp at center. Colors should be slightly warm with the characteristic Petzval contrast — punchy midtones with smooth highlight rolloff. Vignetting should darken the corners naturally.
additionalInstructions: The swirling bokeh pattern must be clearly visible and circular around the subject. The center sharpness must contrast dramatically with the swirling edges. The effect should feel optical, not digital.

name: STREET PHOTOGRAPHY DECISIVE MOMENT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a classic street photograph in the tradition of Henri Cartier-Bresson's 'decisive moment' — the split-second when all elements of a scene align into a perfect composition. The image should feel candid and unposed, captured with a wide-angle or normal lens (35mm or 50mm equivalent) at eye level. The composition should demonstrate geometric awareness: leading lines, reflections, shadows, and human figures all relating to each other in a way that feels both accidental and inevitable. Convert to high-contrast black and white with the grain structure of pushed Tri-X film. The subject should be caught mid-action in an urban environment, with background elements creating visual rhymes or ironic juxtapositions.
additionalInstructions: The moment must feel genuinely decisive — a split-second earlier or later and the composition would fail. The black and white treatment should be contrasty and graphic. The composition should reward extended viewing with discovered relationships between elements.

name: TILT-SHIFT MINIATURE WORLD
message: Take a picture and transform it using extreme tilt-shift photography to make the real world appear as a miniature model or toy set. Apply a very narrow band of sharp focus (simulating an extremely shallow depth of field) with rapid blur falloff above and below. Boost color saturation slightly to mimic the painted quality of model scenery. The viewing angle should be elevated (looking down at approximately 30-45 degrees) as if viewing a model on a table. The subject and their environment should appear toy-like — real but impossibly small, like a perfectly detailed architectural model or train set diorama. Increase contrast slightly and warm the color temperature to enhance the miniature illusion.
additionalInstructions: The narrow focus band must be clearly defined with rapid blur falloff. The elevated angle is essential for the miniature illusion. Color saturation should be boosted but not cartoonish. The subject should appear to be a tiny model figure.

name: COMIC STRIP DAILY
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into the star of a newspaper comic strip — a daily strip with the subject as the recurring main character. The strip should be 3-4 panels telling a complete joke or story beat, drawn in a consistent comic strip style with the subject clearly recognizable throughout. Include the strip title, artist signature, date, and syndication mark. The humor should be character-driven and the art style should be consistent and appealing.

options.text: Classic gag strip — simple setup/punchline, clean lines, Peanuts/Garfield energy
Slice of life — observational humor, relatable situations, Calvin & Hobbes warmth
Absurdist — surreal humor, unexpected turns, Far Side weirdness
Political/editorial — commentary through character, Doonesbury-style wit
Adventure serial — cliffhanger ending, dramatic art, Flash Gordon excitement
Monday morning struggles — the universal dread of the work week beginning
Technology frustration — battling with devices, updates, and digital life
Pet ownership — the joys and absurdities of living with animals
Existential realization — a profound thought hitting at an mundane moment
Social awkwardness — navigating an uncomfortable human interaction

additionalInstructions: The comic strip must tell a complete joke or story in 3-4 panels. The art style must be consistent across all panels. The subject must be clearly recognizable as the main character. The humor should work as an actual comic strip — setup, development, punchline.

name: COLLODION TINTYPE PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a wet plate collodion photograph — the process used from the 1850s-1880s that produces images on glass or metal plates. Show the distinctive wet plate characteristics: slightly uneven coating creating dark edges and flow marks where the collodion was poured, the unique tonal rendering (orthochromatic sensitivity making blue eyes appear light and red lips appear dark), extreme sharpness in the focused area with rapid falloff, and the hand-poured edges of the plate visible as irregular borders. The image should appear on either a dark glass plate (ambrotype) or a blackened metal plate (tintype), with the characteristic creamy highlights and deep blacks of the collodion process.
additionalInstructions: The collodion flow marks and uneven edges are essential characteristics. The orthochromatic tonal rendering must be accurate. The plate edges should be irregular and hand-poured. The overall quality should feel like a genuine 19th-century photograph.

name: HASSELBLAD SPACE PHOTOGRAPHY
message: Take a picture and transform it as if photographed with a Hasselblad camera in space — the same cameras used on NASA missions from Gemini through the Space Shuttle era. The image should have the distinctive qualities of space photography: the medium format square (6x6) frame, Kodak Ektachrome color rendition (slightly cool, highly saturated blues), the absolute black of space as background, the harsh unfiltered sunlight creating extreme contrast with no atmospheric softening, and the slight cross-shaped diffraction spikes on bright highlights from the Zeiss lens. The subject should appear in a space context — floating in microgravity, visible through a spacecraft window, or on a lunar/planetary surface with the characteristic bootprint-sharp shadows of an airless environment.
additionalInstructions: The space lighting must be physically accurate — harsh directional sunlight with no fill from atmosphere. The Hasselblad square format is essential. The Ektachrome color character should be authentic. Include NASA-style frame numbering on the film border.

name: PHOTOJOURNALISM PULITZER
message: Take a picture and transform it into a Pulitzer Prize-worthy photojournalism image — the kind of photograph that captures a universal human moment with such clarity and emotion that it transcends its specific context. The image should be shot in the photojournalist tradition: available light only, no posing or direction, a moment of genuine human emotion or action captured with perfect timing. Convert to high-contrast black and white with the grain of fast film pushed in development (ISO 1600+). The composition should be dynamic but not contrived — the kind of frame that only happens once and requires both preparation and luck to capture. Include a newspaper-style caption with location, date, and wire service credit.
additionalInstructions: The moment must feel genuine and unposed. The technical quality should suggest difficult shooting conditions (available light, fast action). The emotional content should be universal. Include authentic wire service formatting.

name: DREAM CARTOGRAPHY
message: Take a picture and transform it into a map of the subject's dreamscape — a cartographic representation of their subconscious mind rendered as a fantastical territory. The map should use traditional cartographic conventions (compass rose, scale bar, terrain symbols) but chart impossible geography: mountains of memory, rivers of thought, forests of forgotten things, cities built from recurring dreams. The subject's face or form should be subtly integrated into the landscape itself — a mountain range that follows their profile, a coastline that traces their silhouette. The map style should be hand-drawn with watercolor washes, aged parchment, and the ornate decorative elements of Renaissance-era maps including sea monsters and decorative cartouches.
additionalInstructions: The cartographic conventions must be authentic while the geography is impossible. The subject's form should be discoverable within the landscape but not immediately obvious. Place names should be poetic and personal.

name: LIVING CONSTELLATION
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a living constellation — not just stars in the sky but a celestial being made of starlight, nebula gas, and cosmic dust who moves through the universe. The subject should appear as a figure composed of the night sky itself: their body containing galaxies, their eyes burning like binary stars, their hair streaming as comet tails, and their skin showing the deep-field view of distant galaxy clusters. They should appear to be walking through space, leaving trails of stardust, with smaller celestial bodies orbiting them like satellites. The scale should feel cosmic — this being is vast, containing multitudes within their form.
additionalInstructions: The cosmic elements must be astronomically inspired — real nebula colors, actual galaxy shapes, proper star colors based on temperature. The subject must remain recognizable as a figure despite being made of space. The scale should feel infinite.

name: ENCHANTED FOREST SPIRIT
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a forest spirit — a supernatural being that is part of the ancient woodland itself. Their skin should have the texture of birch bark or moss, their hair should be flowing vines and leaves that change with the seasons, their eyes should glow with foxfire (bioluminescent fungal light), and small woodland creatures should rest on their shoulders and in their hair without fear. The forest around them should respond to their presence: flowers blooming where they step, trees bending toward them, fireflies gathering in their wake. The lighting should be the dappled, green-filtered light of a deep old-growth forest with shafts of golden sunlight breaking through the canopy.
additionalInstructions: The natural elements must be botanically real — actual species of moss, lichen, ferns, and fungi. The spirit should feel ancient and benevolent. The forest should feel primeval and magical. Subject identity must be preserved through their features.

name: IMPOSSIBLE ARCHITECTURE
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into an inhabitant of an impossible architectural space — a building that defies physics in the tradition of M.C. Escher's impossible constructions. The subject should be walking on stairs that loop back on themselves, standing in rooms where gravity pulls in multiple directions simultaneously, or looking out windows that show views that shouldn't be possible from their position. The architecture should be rendered in precise, realistic detail (not abstract) making the impossibility more unsettling — every brick, shadow, and perspective line is correct locally but globally contradictory. Other figures in the space should be oriented to different gravitational directions, all equally valid.
additionalInstructions: The impossible geometry must be precisely rendered — each local area should look correct, with the impossibility only apparent when viewing the whole. Shadows and lighting must be locally consistent. The subject should appear unaware of the impossibility.

name: FLOATING ISLAND KINGDOM
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into the ruler or guardian of a floating island kingdom — a fantastical realm of landmasses suspended in the sky, connected by bridges of light, chains, or living vines. The subject should be positioned on the primary island with their kingdom visible around and below them: cascading waterfalls that fall into clouds, inverted mountains hanging beneath islands, vegetation that grows in impossible directions, and smaller satellite islands orbiting the main landmass. The sky should be filled with other distant floating islands at various altitudes, creating a sense of a vast aerial civilization. The lighting should be dramatic — as if the islands exist above the cloud layer in perpetual golden light.
additionalInstructions: The floating islands must feel physically present and massive — not small rocks but entire ecosystems. The subject should appear naturally integrated as an inhabitant of this world. The sense of height and vast open sky should be palpable.

name: TIME FROZEN MOMENT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a moment where time has frozen for everything except the subject. The subject should be the only element in motion (or aware) while everything around them is suspended mid-action: raindrops hanging in the air, birds frozen mid-flight, splashing water suspended in impossible shapes, falling leaves stopped in space, other people frozen mid-stride. The subject should be moving through this frozen world, perhaps reaching out to touch a suspended raindrop or walking between frozen figures. The lighting should emphasize the frozen elements — each suspended droplet catching light like a crystal, each frozen moment preserved in perfect detail.
additionalInstructions: The frozen elements must be physically convincing — water droplets should be the correct shape for their velocity, objects should be frozen in physically accurate mid-motion poses. The subject should be the only source of movement in the frame.

name: PERFUME ADVERTISEMENT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a luxury perfume advertisement — the kind of aspirational, emotionally evocative imagery used to sell high-end fragrances. The subject should be the face of the fragrance, photographed with the ethereal, slightly surreal quality of perfume advertising. Include a perfume bottle design that reflects the fragrance concept, the perfume name in elegant typography, and the overall mood that suggests an invisible scent through purely visual means.

options.text: Fresh/aquatic — water elements, blue tones, ocean spray, clean and invigorating
Floral/romantic — rose petals, soft focus, pink and gold, feminine and timeless
Dark/oriental — amber, smoke, night scenes, mysterious and seductive
Woody/earthy — forest elements, leather, warm browns, grounded and sophisticated
Citrus/energetic — bright colors, dynamic movement, sunshine, youthful and bold
Classic luxury — studio portrait, minimal props, focus on face and bottle, timeless elegance
Narrative/cinematic — suggesting a story, location-based, movie-still quality
Abstract/artistic — surreal elements, unexpected imagery, art-directed concept
Celebrity endorsement — red carpet glamour, fame and aspiration, star power

additionalInstructions: The advertisement must look like a real luxury brand campaign — professional photography, elegant design, aspirational quality. The perfume bottle should be beautifully designed and appropriate to the scent profile. The subject should embody the fragrance's personality. Typography must be luxury-brand quality.

name: MINIATURE CIVILIZATION
message: Take a picture and transform it so that a tiny civilization has built their entire world on and around the subject — treating the subject's body and clothing as their landscape and terrain. Tiny people (1-2mm tall) have constructed villages in the folds of clothing, built bridges across wrinkles, carved homes into buttons, strung lights between hair strands, and established farms on flat surfaces. The miniature civilization should be detailed and thriving — with tiny architecture, infrastructure, agriculture, and daily life all visible upon close inspection. The subject should be unaware of or gently coexisting with their tiny inhabitants. The scale contrast should be dramatic and precisely maintained throughout.
additionalInstructions: The tiny civilization must be internally consistent in scale throughout. The architecture and infrastructure should be detailed enough to suggest a real functioning society. The subject should appear at normal human scale with the tiny world built upon them.

name: MIRROR DIMENSION
message: Take a picture and transform it to show the subject looking into a mirror, but the reflection shows a different version of themselves from a parallel dimension. The 'real' side should be normal and well-lit, while the mirror reflection shows an alternate version — perhaps darker, older, younger, more powerful, more vulnerable, or from a completely different life path. The mirror should be ornate and slightly supernatural (faintly glowing edges, impossible depth, slight rippling of the surface as if liquid). The two versions should be making eye contact through the mirror, creating a moment of recognition between selves. The reflection's world visible behind them should hint at their alternate life.
additionalInstructions: Both versions must be clearly the same person (recognizable subject) but different. The mirror should feel like a genuine portal, not just a reflection. The emotional connection between the two versions should be palpable.

name: UNDERWATER KINGDOM
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into royalty of an underwater kingdom — an Atlantis-like civilization beneath the waves. The subject should appear adapted to aquatic life (subtle gills, slightly iridescent skin, flowing hair that moves as if in water) while wearing elaborate coral and pearl regalia. Their throne room should be visible: architecture grown from living coral, bioluminescent lighting, schools of fish serving as courtiers, and the deep blue-green filtered light of the ocean above. Treasure and artifacts of a sophisticated underwater civilization should surround them. The water should be visible as a medium — particles floating, light rays filtering down from the distant surface, and the slight blue color cast of depth.
additionalInstructions: The underwater physics must be consistent — hair and fabric floating, light filtering correctly for depth, particles suspended in water. The civilization should feel ancient and sophisticated. The subject must remain recognizable with their aquatic adaptations.

name: STEAMPUNK INVENTOR
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a brilliant steampunk inventor in their workshop — surrounded by their impossible brass-and-steam creations. The subject should wear Victorian-era clothing modified with mechanical augmentations: gear-driven monocles, pneumatic arm braces, and tool-laden leather aprons. Their workshop should be filled with half-finished inventions: clockwork automatons, steam-powered computing engines, brass telescopes pointed at impossible things, and blueprints for machines that shouldn't work but clearly do. The lighting should be warm gaslight supplemented by the glow of furnaces and electrical arcs. Every surface should be covered in tools, parts, and the organized chaos of genius at work.
additionalInstructions: The steampunk technology must feel functional and internally consistent — not just decorative gears but purposeful mechanisms. The Victorian aesthetic must be authentic. The subject should appear as a genius in their element. Preserve subject identity clearly.

name: ASTRAL PROJECTION
message: Take a picture and transform it to show the subject in a state of astral projection — their luminous spirit form rising from or floating above their physical body. The physical body should be in a meditative pose, peaceful and still, while the astral form above is translucent, glowing with inner light, and connected to the body by a thin silver cord. The astral form should be slightly idealized — the same person but radiating peace and power, perhaps with visible chakra points glowing along their spine. The astral plane around the spirit form should be different from the physical world — more colorful, with visible energy flows, sacred geometry patterns in the air, and a sense of infinite space beyond the physical room's walls.
additionalInstructions: Both the physical body and astral form must be clearly the same person. The astral form should be luminous and translucent but clearly defined. The silver cord connecting them should be visible. The two planes of existence should be visually distinct.

name: BOOK PORTAL
message: Take a picture and transform it to show the subject being pulled into (or emerging from) the pages of a giant open book. The book should be enormous — large enough for a person to fall into — and the pages should be transforming from flat text and illustrations into a three-dimensional world as the subject crosses the threshold. On the book side, words should be lifting off pages and becoming the objects they describe, illustrations should be gaining depth and color, and the flat page should be curving into a horizon. The subject should be mid-transition — partially in the real world, partially in the story world — with their appearance changing as they cross (gaining armor, wings, a crown, or whatever the story demands).
additionalInstructions: The transition from 2D page to 3D world must be seamless and visually clear. Text becoming objects should be readable at the word-to-thing transition point. The subject should be recognizable in both their real and story-world versions.

name: CRYSTAL CAVE GUARDIAN
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into the ancient guardian of a crystal cave — a being who has spent so long among the crystals that they have partially crystallized themselves. Their skin should show areas of crystal growth — amethyst, quartz, selenite, and fluorite formations emerging from their body as if growing naturally. Their eyes should be faceted like gemstones, refracting light into rainbow spectrums. The cave around them should be filled with enormous crystal formations in impossible colors, each emitting its own soft light. The guardian should appear both ancient and timeless — neither young nor old but mineral, patient, and eternal. Light should refract through their crystalline portions, casting colored patterns on the cave walls.
additionalInstructions: The crystal formations must be mineralogically inspired — real crystal shapes and growth patterns. The integration of crystal and flesh should be seamless and beautiful, not grotesque. The cave lighting should come primarily from the crystals themselves. Subject identity must be preserved.

name: CYBERPUNK STREET SAMURAI
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a cyberpunk street samurai — a high-tech warrior of the neon-lit urban future. The subject should have visible cybernetic augmentations: a glowing cybernetic eye, neural interface ports, a mechanical arm with visible servos, and subdermal armor plating. Their clothing should be a mix of tactical gear and street fashion — armored jacket with holographic patches, LED-threaded fabric, and concealed weapon sheaths. The environment should be a rain-slicked alley in a mega-city: towering buildings covered in holographic advertisements, neon signs in multiple languages, steam rising from grates, and the ever-present rain reflecting all the artificial light. The color palette should be dominated by neon cyan, magenta, and electric blue against deep shadows.
additionalInstructions: The cybernetic augmentations must look functional and integrated, not just decorative. The urban environment must feel lived-in and detailed. The neon lighting should be the primary light source, creating colored shadows. Subject identity must be preserved despite augmentations.

name: POCKET DIMENSION
message: Take a picture and transform it to show the subject holding or opening a small object (a locket, a music box, a snow globe, a pocket watch) that contains an entire world inside it. The object should be realistically sized in their hands, but when opened or looked into, it reveals an impossibly vast landscape, city, or universe contained within. The interior world should be detailed and alive — with weather, inhabitants, architecture, and its own light source. The contrast between the small container and the vast world within should be the central visual tension. Light from the interior world should spill out, illuminating the subject's face with otherworldly colors.
additionalInstructions: The scale contrast must be dramatic and clear — tiny container, vast world within. The interior world must be detailed enough to feel real and inhabited. The light spilling from the object should illuminate the subject's face. Subject must be clearly recognizable.

name: CHILDREN'S TV SHOW CHARACTER
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a character from a children's educational TV show — the kind of bright, friendly, engaging character designed to teach young viewers. The subject should be rendered in the appropriate animation or puppet style, placed in the show's colorful set or world, with educational elements visible. The character should feel warm, approachable, and designed to hold a child's attention while teaching something.

options.text: Puppet/Muppet style — felt and foam construction, expressive eyes, colorful set pieces
2D animation — bright flat colors, simple shapes, smooth movement, friendly design
3D CGI — rounded forms, soft textures, Pixar-junior quality, tactile and warm
Live action with animation — real person in animated world, mixed media magic
Stop motion — clay or felt figures, handmade charm, slightly imperfect and lovable
Letters and reading — alphabet elements, books, word-building, literacy adventure
Numbers and math — counting objects, shapes, patterns, mathematical discovery
Science and nature — magnifying glass, plants, animals, curiosity and exploration
Social-emotional learning — feelings faces, friendship scenarios, kindness themes
Music and movement — instruments, dance, rhythm, creative expression

additionalInstructions: The character design must be genuinely appealing to young children — friendly, non-threatening, and engaging. The educational elements should be naturally integrated, not forced. The subject must be recognizable despite the stylistic transformation. The overall tone should be warm and encouraging.

name: LIVING PAINTING ESCAPE
message: Take a picture and transform it to show the subject escaping from a painting — literally climbing out of a framed canvas that hangs on a gallery wall. The subject should be mid-emergence: their upper body in the real three-dimensional gallery space (fully rendered, photorealistic) while their lower body is still within the painting (rendered in the painting's style — oil paint, visible brushstrokes, flat perspective). The transition zone where they cross the frame should show the fascinating moment where painted brushstrokes become real flesh, where flat color becomes three-dimensional form. Paint should be dripping from their emerging form. The gallery around them should be realistic, with other paintings on the walls and proper museum lighting.
additionalInstructions: The transition from painted to real must be seamless and visually fascinating. The painting style should be clearly different from the photorealistic gallery space. The frame should be a physical boundary being crossed. Subject identity must be clear in both the painted and real versions.

name: KOLROSING WOOD TECHNIQUE
message: Take a picture and transform it into a kolrosing artwork — the traditional Scandinavian technique of scoring fine lines into wood and rubbing them with coffee grounds, charcoal, or bark dust to create delicate illustrations on birch or pine surfaces. The image should show the subject rendered in extremely fine scored lines on a pale wood surface, with the natural wood grain visible beneath and interacting with the design. The lines should have the characteristic quality of a knife-scored surface — thin, precise, and slightly irregular where the blade followed the grain. The overall effect should be subtle and elegant, like a whispered drawing on living wood.
additionalInstructions: The wood grain must be visible and interact naturally with the scored design. The lines should be fine and precise. The overall effect should be subtle — dark lines on pale wood. Subject identity must be preserved.

name: CHIAROSCURO WOODCUT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a chiaroscuro woodcut — the Renaissance technique using multiple wood blocks printed in sequence to create tonal depth. The image should show 3-4 distinct tonal layers: a key block providing the darkest outlines and shadows, and 2-3 tone blocks in progressively lighter values (typically warm browns, ochres, or olive greens). The paper tone serves as the lightest value. Each layer should be slightly misregistered (as in authentic historical prints) creating a subtle dimensional effect. The subject should emerge dramatically from shadow in the manner of Ugo da Carpi or Hans Baldung Grien.
additionalInstructions: The multiple block layers must be distinguishable. Slight misregistration between layers adds authenticity. The limited color palette (3-4 tones plus paper) must create convincing depth. Subject must be clearly recognizable.

name: SAND PAINTING CEREMONY
message: Take a picture and transform it into a sand painting — the sacred art form using colored sand, crushed minerals, and natural pigments carefully placed grain by grain on a flat surface. The subject should be rendered in the geometric, symbolic style of sand painting traditions, with bold colors (turquoise, coral, white, black, yellow) creating the image through precise placement of colored granules. The texture should clearly show individual grains of sand at close inspection. The composition should be symmetrical and ceremonial, with the subject integrated into a larger symbolic design featuring directional guardians, sacred mountains, and rainbow borders.
additionalInstructions: The sand texture must be visible — individual grains should be suggested. Colors should be those achievable with natural minerals. The composition should feel ceremonial and balanced. Subject identity should be preserved within the symbolic style.

name: HINTERGLASMALEREI FOLK ART
message: Take a picture and transform it into a reverse glass painting (verre églomisé) — the folk art technique of painting on the back of glass so the image is viewed through the glass surface. The painting should show the characteristic qualities: slightly flattened perspective, bold outlines painted first (since you work in reverse order), vibrant colors that appear luminous behind glass, and the occasional gold or silver leaf background. The glass surface should show slight reflections and the depth between the viewer and the painted surface. The style should be folk art — charming, slightly naive, with decorative borders and floral embellishments typical of European or Asian reverse glass traditions.
additionalInstructions: The reverse painting technique means details are painted first, backgrounds last — this creates a distinctive layered look. The glass surface should be subtly visible. Colors should be bold and luminous. Subject must be recognizable in the folk art style.

name: EGGSHELL MOSAIC
message: Take a picture and transform it into an eggshell mosaic — the delicate art of creating images from carefully placed fragments of dyed eggshell on a dark background. Each tiny piece of shell should be visible as a distinct curved fragment, with the dark gaps between pieces creating a natural network of fine lines (similar to crackle glaze). The eggshell pieces should be dyed in various colors to create the image, with the natural curve and texture of shell visible in each fragment. The overall effect should be intricate and precious — like a Byzantine mosaic rendered in the most fragile of materials.
additionalInstructions: Individual eggshell fragments must be visible with dark gaps between them. The natural curve of shell pieces should be apparent. The fragility of the medium should be evident. Subject must be clearly recognizable through the mosaic pattern.

name: SMOKE ART PHOTOGRAPHY
message: Take a picture and transform it so the subject appears to be formed entirely from wisps of smoke against a pure black background. The smoke should be photographed with the precision of high-speed smoke photography — sharp, detailed, showing the complex turbulent flow patterns of real smoke. The subject's form should be suggested through the natural curling and folding of smoke tendrils, with some areas dense and defined while others trail off into wisps. The smoke should be lit from the side to create maximum texture and depth. Colors should be limited to the natural palette of smoke photography — white, gray, and subtle warm tones from the light source — unless colored smoke is used for specific features.
additionalInstructions: The smoke must look physically real — following actual fluid dynamics. The subject should be recognizable but ethereal. The black background must be absolute. Lighting should create maximum texture in the smoke.

name: LINOCUT REDUCTION PRINT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a reduction linocut print — the technique where a single block is progressively carved and printed in multiple colors, from lightest to darkest. The image should show 4-6 distinct color layers, each with the characteristic carved texture of linoleum (smooth curves, bold shapes, visible gouge marks). Since each color is printed over the previous ones, the layering should be visible where colors overlap. The style should be bold and graphic — reduction linocuts demand confident design decisions since each cut is irreversible. The subject should be simplified into strong shapes with clear color separation.
additionalInstructions: The carved linoleum texture must be visible in each color layer. The progressive layering from light to dark should be apparent. Bold, confident shapes are essential. Subject must be recognizable through the simplified graphic treatment.

name: PAPER QUILLING PORTRAIT
message: Take a picture and transform it into a paper quilling artwork — the art of rolling, shaping, and arranging thin strips of paper into intricate designs. The subject should be constructed entirely from coiled, scrolled, and shaped paper strips viewed from above, creating a relief sculpture effect. Different quilling shapes (tight coils, loose coils, teardrops, marquises, hearts, scrolls) should be used to create different textures and tonal values. The paper strips should be visible on their edges, creating fine lines of color. The three-dimensional quality of the coils should cast subtle shadows, adding depth to the portrait.
additionalInstructions: Individual paper coils and shapes must be clearly visible. The 3D relief quality should be apparent through shadows. Different quilling shapes should create varied textures. Subject identity must be preserved through careful arrangement of shapes.

name: ZODIAC WARRIOR
message: Take a picture and transform the subject into a celestial warrior embodying their zodiac sign — a powerful figure whose armor, weapons, and powers are derived from their astrological symbol. The warrior should be depicted in a dramatic battle-ready pose with constellation patterns glowing on their armor, celestial weapons drawn, and their zodiac animal or symbol manifesting as a spirit companion or power source. The background should be a cosmic battlefield — stars, nebulae, and celestial phenomena creating an epic arena.
